In the top-events branch that rewritten list is passed as timeseries_columns / y_axes, but orderby=self.get_orderby(request) is left unchanged, so a normal sort=-count() still ranks groups by the raw count() aggregate while the plotted series is upsampled_count() as count. Top-N groups are chosen by sampled volume, so a low sample rate and high true volume group can be omitted; if the builder treats ORDER BY count() as a different aggregate from the alias, the top-events query errors instead. Equations (equation|count() * 2 and get_equation_list) and aggregate conditions in the query string (count():>N) are not rewritten either, so filters and equation series do not match the upsampled count series. Other count-derived y-axes such as epm() and eps() stay sampled, so one response can show an upsampled count beside a sampled rate. Columns that are already aliased, such as count() as errors, also fail the exact match and silently skip upsampling.

Shared cache around an in-memory option read slows and can fail stats

is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects calls cache.get and cache.set on Sentry's shared cache (Redis in production) on every events-stats query, including each dashboard split subquery, to avoid options.get of issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist. That option read is already a process-local dict lookup, so the cache adds a network round trip on a hot endpoint instead of removing work. Cache errors are not caught here, and OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint does not catch them either, so a Redis timeout fails the chart. Keys are one per organization plus hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))), which is high-cardinality, and Python hash() is not a collision-resistant digest, so a collision would reuse another project set's allowlist boolean and could enable sum(sample_weight) for a set that is not fully allowlisted. invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called and can delete only one exact key, so it does not flush eligibility after an allowlist change. The docstring on _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, which says each call reads the latest configuration, is false once this 60-second cache is in front of it.

Upsampled count sums sample_weight but nothing stores that weight

upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) and is substituted for count() on allowlisted error queries. This change never writes sample_weight and never computes an inverse sample rate. The only data-path edit, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling in the test factory, copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate (for example 0.1) onto the existing event field sample_rate, which is the server-side sampling rate, not a weight. ClickHouse sum skips nulls, and the aggregate does not use ifNull(sample_weight, 1), so events with a missing weight contribute nothing; toInt64 then truncates a fractional sum toward zero, so a stored rate of 0.1 becomes 0 rather than 10. OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint only catches ValidationError, so if sample_weight is absent on the queried entity the chart request 500s instead of falling back to count(). The new stats test expects each 0.1-sampled event to contribute 10, which this code cannot produce. Once the allowlist is non-empty, error count charts for those projects will be zeroed, truncated, or failed.

Upsampling tests assert a 10x count the fixtures never produce

test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects stores events with client_sample_rate 0.1 and asserts each bucket count is 10. The factory only sets sample_rate to 0.1 and never sets sample_weight to 10, and no test inspects the SnQL or the stored column, so the assertion does not prove upsampling and fails unless an out-of-diff processor inverts the rate. The unit tests never call is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, never seed or clear the new cache, and never cover !event.type:error, mixed event.type:error OR event.type:transaction, dataset=errors (which the helper always rewrites), events missing sample_weight, or topEvents sorted by count(). Those are the paths that currently mis-apply or skip the rewrite.

upsampled_count is a public discover aggregate and bypasses the allowlist

upsampled_count is registered on Discover's function converter without private=True, unlike the neighboring function in the same list (private defaults to false). It therefore becomes a user-facing function on every discover endpoint that shares this converter, not only the allowlisted stats path. Clients can request yAxis=upsampled_count(), or use it in other discover and alert queries, for projects that are not allowlisted and for queries that include transactions. The aggregate itself has no allowlist or dataset guard and always emits sum(sample_weight), so a missing column becomes a Snuba error and the gate in organization_events_stats is bypassable. It also sets default_result_type to number while count() is an integer, so series metadata changes type. If private functions are rejected by the same column parser the stats rewrite uses, marking it private will 400 the rewrite; the weight sum should be applied inside the query builder under the allowlist check rather than exposed as a public function.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Flagged table widgets render an empty hardcoded table

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `tableResultComponent` ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, column fields, aliases, and the loading state and instead renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and `tableData.data: []`. An empty `columns` array is truthy, so the visualization will not infer columns from meta either. Any org with that flag on sees blank dashboard table widgets instead of the query results.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity refresh batch

`check_auth_identities` now has `processing_deadline_duration=60`, but `check_auth` still enqueues up to `chunk_size` (default 100) identities and this task refreshes them sequentially via external IdP calls. That routinely exceeds 60s. `check_auth` already sets `last_synced=now` before the task runs, so if the worker kills the task and does not retry the same id list, the unfinished identities are skipped until the next ~24h cycle and SSO validity is not refreshed. If it does retry, the same chunk keeps timing out and hammering the IdP.

Custom cell renderers cannot return falsy nodes

Both head and body renderers treat any falsy return as "use the fallback" (`if (cell)`), but the documented contract is that only `undefined` means fallback. A custom renderer that returns `0`, `''`, or `null` (valid React output, and a reasonable way to blank a cell) is discarded and the default field renderer runs instead.

Error IDs are queried with page-filter dates the AI tab never sends

Error IDs now come from `query_replay_instance` using `start`/`end` from `get_filter_params(request, project)`. Segment loading (`fetch_segments_metadata`) does not use that window. The replay AI tab calls `/replays/{id}/summarize/breadcrumbs/` with no `statsPeriod`, `start`, or `end`. Depending on the default stats period, either the request 400s (breaking an endpoint that previously did not need dates) or error lookup is limited to a window shorter than replay retention, so older replays are summarized with no error context while their breadcrumbs still load.

Error events are not ordered against replay segment timestamps

Chronological merge compares nodestore `timestamp` (unix seconds, and sometimes an ISO-8601 string) with the raw segment event `timestamp`. Recording segments are rrweb payloads whose timestamps are milliseconds. A seconds value is always less than a millisecond timestamp, so every error is emitted before every breadcrumb; if the stored timestamp is a string, `str < float` raises TypeError and the summarize request 500s. That is a regression for replays that have linked errors, because this endpoint previously summarized breadcrumbs without this comparison. The unit test avoids it by fabricating segment timestamps in seconds.

Feedback summary ignores the environment page filter

The summary request sends the normalized datetime and `selection.projects`, but not `selection.environments`. The feedback list page is wrapped in page filters, so the list and search respect the environment selector while the summary does not. A user filtered to one environment still gets a summary of feedback from every environment in the project/date range, which can contradict the list beside it.

Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching

`HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is applied only inside the `searchQuery` branch. When the search box is empty the function returns `sortAttributes(attributes)` unfiltered, so those fields still render. When the user searches, the same names are excluded even if the query matches them. The hide list needs to apply before the search filter, not instead of the unfiltered list.

Replay error context reads title/message that stored events do not have

`fetch_error_details` builds the Seer log from `data.get("title")` and `data.get("message")` on the raw nodestore payload. Stored error events usually keep the exception under `exception.values` / `metadata` (`type` and `value`); `title` is computed on the Event model and is often absent, and `message` is frequently empty. The log becomes `User experienced an error: ': ' at ...`, so exception type and value never reach the summary. The new test expects `ZeroDivisionError` and `division by zero` in that log after storing an exception-only event, which this field choice does not produce.

Report URL validation rejects real browser documents and aborts the batch

`url` is a DRF `URLField`, whose default validator only allows http(s)/ftp. Reporting API document URLs include `about:blank`, `blob:`, `chrome-extension:`, and `file:` URLs, so those reports fail validation. The handler then returns 422 on the first invalid item and does not record metrics for any later valid reports in the same array. Browsers post mixed batches, and the previous dataclass path accepted unknown types and non-http URLs and still counted them.

Suspect-issue PR comments call helpers that are not on the workflow class

`get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` and `get_environment_info` are defined on `CommitContextIntegration` (the class that ends just before `OpenPRCommentWorkflow`), but `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` call them as `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` / `self.get_environment_info(issue)`. Those workflow classes subclass `PRCommentWorkflow`, which holds an integration rather than inheriting these methods. The static helper also does `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, and `_truncate_title` is not defined on `PRCommentWorkflow`. Generating a merged-PR suspect-issue comment therefore raises AttributeError, so the GitHub/GitLab comment task fails and no comment is posted.

Trace waterfall wrapper dropped height: 100%

The waterfall root was a flex column with `flex-grow: 1` and `height: 100%`. It is now `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>`, which does not set `height: 100%`. The trace view sizes this pane with a height chain rather than only flex-grow, so the waterfall can collapse and the virtualized span tree no longer fills the viewport.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Valid backup codes are rejected unless they match lowercase hex exactly

Stored codes are lowercase hex from `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`. Login compares with `indexOf` after removing only "-" characters. The same check is in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` at the `replaceAll("-", "")` / `indexOf` call. There is no `toLowerCase()` or trim. The entry field (`apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx`) uses placeholder "XXXXX-XXXXX", which reads as uppercase, and does not set `autoCapitalize="none"` or `autoCorrect="off"`, so mobile keyboards will capitalize the first character. Pasting a line from the downloaded file often includes a trailing newline or space; a code entered as uppercase or with whitespace will not match and the user gets "incorrect backup code" for a real code. Normalize by stripping whitespace and dashes and lowercasing before compare, on both login and disable.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One-time backup codes can be replayed or restored under concurrent logins

After a backup code matches, the handler nulls that array slot and writes the re-encrypted list with a plain `prisma.user.update` on user id. The read, check, and write are not in a transaction and the update is not conditional on the previous ciphertext. Two parallel logins with the same code can both see it as unused and both receive sessions. Two parallel logins with different codes can also lose an update: the later write is based on a stale array and can put a just-consumed code back. Backup codes are documented as single-use, but that is not enforced. Consume the code with a row lock or compare-and-swap on the stored ciphertext so only one request can spend a given code.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code alone can log in if any TOTP field is sent

Password verification in credentials authorize runs only when `user.password` is set and `credentials.totpCode` is empty. The new branch then treats any non-empty `backupCode` as a full login: it decrypts the stored codes, and on a match it burns that code and returns a session. It never checks the password itself. A caller who knows only a backup code (the plaintext file this feature downloads as cal-backup-codes.txt, a clipboard copy, or the setup response) can POST email, `totpCode` set to any non-empty value such as "1", and that backup code, and get a session without the password. The normal UI often avoids this only because it clears `totpCode` before submit; the credentials endpoint does not. The code is also consumed on that request, so the attacker takes the account and destroys a recovery code. Verify the password inside this branch whenever the user has one, before accepting or burning the code. Do not rely on the earlier `!credentials.totpCode` gate.

Closing the backup-code dialog does not finish setup or keep the codes

TOTP enable is committed on the server before the backup codes are shown (`setStep(DisplayBackupCodes)` only after enable returns 200). The plaintext codes exist only in that earlier setup response and in React state; nothing in this PR can show them again, and `setup.ts` rejects another setup with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled once 2FA is on. The dialog still uses the parent `onOpenChange` with no guard. Cancel is hidden on this step, but Escape, overlay click, and the dialog close control still dismiss it. Only the Close button calls `onEnable()` (and `resetState()`). The new e2e expects the security switch to become checked only after that Close click, so a dismiss leaves the settings UI showing 2FA off while the account has 2FA on. If the modal unmounts or the user leaves the page without using Copy/Download, the codes are gone and cannot be recovered without the authenticator. Block dismiss on this step until the user confirms the codes are saved, or call the same completion path as Close, and offer a way to regenerate codes while 2FA is already on.

Copy toast claims success even if clipboard write fails

The Copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` and immediately shows the success toast without awaiting or catching the promise. `writeText` rejects when clipboard permission is denied, the document is not focused, or `navigator.clipboard` is unavailable, and that rejection is unhandled. The user is told "Backup codes copied!" and can close the only screen that shows the codes without a copy actually existing. Await the write, and show an error toast (and do not claim success) if it fails.

Missing-backup-codes error points at a settings flow that does not exist

The new string is "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Login and disable show it when 2FA is on and `backupCodes` is null (every account that enabled 2FA before this migration, and any account whose codes were never stored). There is no settings control or API in this PR to generate codes afterward: `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled if 2FA is already on, and codes are only returned during that setup call. A user who lost the authenticator and follows this message cannot generate codes and cannot sign in. The copy should not tell them to do something the product cannot do.

Tests never prove a backup code can log in or that it is single-use

The first enable test still ends by waiting on the 2FA switch after OTP submit and does not click `backup-codes-close`. After this PR that submit leaves the backup-code dialog open and does not run `onEnable`, so the switch is not updated; the assertion above is the one the new FIXME says passes even when the switch is unchecked. The second test only checks that a download is named cal-backup-codes.txt, that a success toast appears, and that Close checks the switch. It does not read the file or clipboard (those checks are TODOs) and never submits a backup code. Nothing covers login with a backup code, rejection of a wrong or reused code, or disabling 2FA with a backup code, which is the behavior this PR adds. A break in comparison, consumption, or the password check would still leave CI green.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet fallback throws when no destination calendar is set

The Meet-without-Google-Calendar fallback used to read destinationCalendar?.integration, so a missing calendar evaluated to undefined and was replaced with Cal Video. It now destructures the first element of the new array and reads .integration with no null check. handleNewBooking sets destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and confirm.handler sets []. Both become an empty array here, so mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and booking creation throws TypeError before the fallback can run. Any Google Meet booking that has no destination calendar — the case this branch exists for — now fails instead of falling back to Cal Video.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update/delete fallback compares externalId to a missing id

When externalCalendarId is missing, updateEvent used to fall back to destinationCalendar.externalId. It now does destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). That find only runs when externalCalendarId is already null or empty, so it looks for a calendar whose externalId is null and never matches. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined and the update fails. deleteEvent (line 317) has the same find, then falls back to "primary", so a cancellation of an event that lives on a non-primary calendar and whose booking reference has no externalCalendarId hits primary, gets a 404, and is swallowed — the event stays on the user's calendar and continues to block time. Fall back to the destination entry for this credential, or to destinationCalendar[0].externalId, not to a comparison against the missing id.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug is now set in the opposite billing case

This unrelated edit inverts when an organization slug is stored. Previously slug was written on the team when team billing was disabled, and only metadata.requestedSlug was stored when billing was enabled so the slug could be assigned after payment. The new condition sets slug only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, and sets nothing when it is false. The requestedSlug line was not inverted, so billing-enabled creates now set both slug and requestedSlug. Self-hosted orgs (billing flag off) are created with no slug and cannot be resolved by subdomain. Billing-enabled orgs claim the slug immediately while still unverified, which conflicts with the deferred-slug flow. Restore slug when billing is disabled, and only requestedSlug when it is enabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
A missing calendar credential fails every calendar update

The new update loop loads a credential by reference.credentialId, but if it is still missing (deleted credential, or app.slug absent so the DB object is ignored) it still calls updateEvent(credential, ...) with credential undefined. createAllCalendarEvents guards with if (credential); this path does not. updateEvent then rejects, Promise.all rejects, and the catch treats every calendar reference as failed even if other updates already ran. The catch builds an error message and no longer logs it (console.error was removed), so the failure is silent in logs. Skip or record a per-reference failure when the credential cannot be loaded, and do not abort the rest of the batch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancelling a recurring series does not delete co-host calendar events

When all remaining instances of a recurring booking are cancelled, the new per-reference loop still uses the old recurring body. That body ignores the reference and credential just resolved (including a co-host credential loaded from the database) and instead walks only the booking owner's calendar credentials. For each instance it uses references.find, so only the first calendar reference is deleted, and that delete is repeated once per owner credential and once per outer reference. Co-host credentials are never used, so their events stay on their calendars and keep blocking availability after the series is cancelled. Delete every calendar reference of every updated instance with that reference's own credentialId, and do not nest that work inside the outer reference loop.

Collective host calendars are discarded when the main calendar is null

Co-host destination calendars are collected into teamDestinationCalendars, then appended with evt.destinationCalendar?.push. The field is set to null when the event type and the organizer both lack a destination calendar, and optional push on null does nothing, so every co-host calendar just collected is dropped. createAllCalendarEvents then sees no destinations. Its empty-list fallback only keeps credentials whose type is exactly "calendar", which never matches real types such as google_calendar, so nobody gets a calendar event. Even when the array is non-null, a host is included only if user.destinationCalendar is already set and schedulingType is COLLECTIVE, so a connected calendar with no destination-calendar row, and dynamic multi-user bookings without that scheduling type, still never get events. Initialize an array before pushing, and do not rely on the null optional chain.

Confirming a collective booking still schedules one calendar

confirmHandler builds the CalendarEvent passed to handleConfirmation with only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar, wrapped in a one-element array. Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation (handleNewBooking connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]), and this handler never loads the other hosts' destination calendars. handleConfirmation is not updated in this PR to expand hosts itself, so a collective event that requires confirmation still creates a calendar event only for that one calendar. Co-hosts do not get events on confirm, which is the bug this change is supposed to fix for any booking that is not immediately accepted.

Each host create still targets only the first destination calendar

createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination, but always passes the original event whose destinationCalendar array still lists every host. Lark (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts around line 129), Office 365 (office365calendar CalendarService.ts around line 75), and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 162) only read index 0. Later iterations therefore use the co-host's token against the first host's calendar id. Office 365 and Lark fail that write; CalDAV filters to the foreign URL, matches nothing, and still returns a successful uid, so a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. The no-credentialId branch at line 380 also calls createEvent without destination.externalId and for every credential of that integration type, which duplicates events and cannot reach other hosts' credentials. If a credential cannot be loaded or has no app.slug, that host is skipped with no error result, so the booking still succeeds. updateAllCalendarEvents (line 542) passes the same unsplit event into every update, so reschedule has the same index-0 problem whenever a service falls back to destinationCalendar[0]. This is the stated acceptance criterion (every host calendar app should receive the event) and it does not hold for non-Google calendars.

Google organizer email is always the first destination calendar

createEvent now picks the calendar to write by matching credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still taken from destinationCalendar[0] (mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId). The same event object, containing every host, is passed on every call, so an event written onto a co-host's calendar lists the primary host's calendar externalId as organizer. updateEvent (line 228) does the same on reschedule and location updates. Google can reject a write whose organizer does not match the authenticated calendar, or save an event with the wrong organizer and guest list, so co-host Google events are wrong even when calendarId selection succeeds. Select the destination entry that matches the credential or externalCalendarId being written, or pass a one-element destinationCalendar for that host.

Location change saves calendar references without calendar ids

updateLocation builds referencesToCreate from result.externalId and result.credentialId. Calendar updates come from updateEvent, whose EventResult does not set externalId, credentialId, or createdEvent (CalendarManager.updateEvent only returns updatedEvent). Previously this mapping copied evt.destinationCalendar.externalId and credentialId onto every new reference. editLocation.handler persists referencesToCreate with references.create, so each location edit now inserts calendar rows with an empty uid and no externalCalendarId or credentialId. Later cancel/update cannot target the calendar those rows refer to, and deleteEvent may be called with an empty uid. Copy the reference's existing externalCalendarId and credentialId (or return them from updateEvent) instead of reading fields update results do not populate.

Merging a reschedule deletes only the first old calendar event

When newBookingId is set, updateAllCalendarEvents now updates every calendar reference, but the following cleanup still uses booking.references.find for a single _calendar reference and deletes only that one, and only if it has a credentialId. Co-host events created by this PR are left on their calendars after a seated merge/reschedule, so those slots stay busy. If the first reference has no credentialId, none of the old events are deleted. Delete every old calendar reference, using each reference's credentialId.

New booking references drop video credentialId and some external calendar ids

referencesToCreate used to store evt.destinationCalendar.externalId for calendar results and result.credentialId for non-calendar results. It now stores result.externalId and, for anything that is not a calendar type, hardcodes credentialId to undefined. createAllCalendarEvents only passes destination.externalId into createEvent when destination.credentialId is set (line 370). The legacy branch at line 380 calls createEvent(c, event) with no external id, so those references are saved with externalCalendarId undefined. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference's credentialId is set, so if the video EventResult carried credentialId — which this mapping used to persist — cancelling a booking no longer deletes the remote meeting. Calendar references missing externalCalendarId also cannot be updated or deleted on the right calendar, especially with the broken Google fallback.

No test covers multi-host calendar create, update, or delete

The only test change rewrites the BOOKING_REJECTED webhook fixture from destinationCalendar null to []. There is no coverage that a collective booking writes an event to each host's calendar, stores a reference with that host's credentialId and externalCalendarId, updates those events on reschedule, and deletes all of them on cancel — including non-Google calendars, a missing organizer destination calendar, recurring cancel-all, and payment or confirmation flows. The PR checklist notes that no such test was added. The bugs in this change (null push dropping co-host calendars, services always using index 0, recurring cancel deleting only the first reference) would not be caught in CI.

PayPal confirmation creates events for only one calendar

On payment success this builds evt.destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner's user.destinationCalendar only, then, when the booking is already accepted, calls eventManager.create(evt). That is a single calendar. The in-memory multi-host list from handleNewBooking is not stored on the booking (only the first destination calendar is connected), and this webhook does not load event-type hosts. Paid collective bookings whose calendar events are created here still invite only one host.

Reschedule request deletes co-host events with the acting user's token

Requesting a reschedule cancels the booking and deletes calendar events, but credentials are keyed only by credential.type from the acting user (credentialsMap.set(credential.type, credential)), not by reference.credentialId. A co-host reference whose type the actor also has (for example google_calendar) is deleted with the actor's token and the co-host's event uid. Google treats the resulting 404 as success, so the co-host event is left in place and the slot stays busy. References whose type the actor does not have are skipped entirely, with no database credential lookup. handleCancelBooking was updated to delete each reference with its own credential; this path was not, so collective events created by this PR are not removed from co-host calendars when a reschedule is requested.

Stripe confirmation creates events for only one calendar

handlePaymentSuccess sets destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner only, then calls eventManager.create(evt) when the booking is already accepted. getBooking (line 119) does the same, and handleSetupSuccess uses that evt to create events when confirmation is not required. Neither path loads other collective hosts' destination calendars, and the booking row only has the first destination calendar connected. Paid or setup-intent collective bookings therefore still create a calendar event for one host only.

Webhook destinationCalendar changed from object to array

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now DestinationCalendar[] | null, and webhook payloads spread that evt (the playwright BOOKING_* assertions include this field). Existing consumers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will get undefined, because those fields are on the object, not the array. The PR describes this as a non-breaking bugfix, but it is a public payload break with no versioning. Producers are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking sends null when unset, while confirm and the payment webhooks send []. BOOKING_REJECTED in webhook.e2e.ts now expects [] and BOOKING_CREATED / BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect null, so clients cannot null-check the field reliably.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Refresh parser invents refresh_token and strips real token fields

After a successful parse, parseRefreshTokenResponse sets data.refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the field is missing, and callers persist that object. Office365CalendarService spreads the parsed data over the stored credential. Its schema marks refresh_token optional, and Microsoft's token endpoint is allowed to omit a new refresh token while the previous one stays valid. The spread then replaces the real refresh token with "refresh_token", so the next refresh fails until the user reconnects. This is not limited to the new sync flag. When sharing is enabled the schema used instead is also wrong: the computed keys z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() are one literal property (both are typically "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first), not a wildcard, and Zod strips unknown keys. expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, scope, and instance_url are dropped, then the placeholder refresh token is added. Office 365 and Zoom write that result back; Zoom also sets expiry_date from a missing expires_in, which is NaN, and zoomTokenSchema rejects NaN on the next read. Salesforce would persist the stripped object once its missing prisma import is fixed. The comment that any numeric property is the expiry is not implemented.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google refresh persists the Zod wrapper and breaks the credential

GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken now saves the return value of parseRefreshTokenResponse as credential.key. That helper returns Zod's safeParse result, {success: true, data: ...}, not the token object. The previous code stored googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials). This runs on every expiry refresh whether or not credential sharing is enabled. After the first successful refresh (access tokens last about an hour), the row no longer matches googleCredentialSchema, which is parsed again in the constructor at the next GoogleCalendarService load. Availability, event create/update/delete, and Meet links then throw for that linked credential. Reconnecting creates a new credential row and does not repair the existing id already attached to destination calendars, so the broken row keeps being selected. When sharing is enabled the same function fails earlier: refreshOAuthTokens returns a Fetch Response with no .data, token.access_token throws, and the catch treats every error other than invalid_grant as success and returns the expired client without writing a new token.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync refresh returns an unchecked Fetch Response that callers treat as a provider token

When sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw Fetch Response and does not check response.ok, parse JSON, or set a timeout. Callers were not updated to that contract, and the comment says the body should only be an access token and expiry, which is not what they read. HubSpot, Zoho CRM, and Zoho Bigin expect an axios or HubSpot SDK object and read .data, .accessToken, or .expiresIn. HubSpot then passes that Response to prisma.credential.update as key; JSON serialization keeps only the own property expiryDate (NaN becomes null), so the stored HubSpot credential is wiped to {expiryDate: null}. Google reads res.data, throws, and its catch swallows every error except invalid_grant, leaving the expired token in place. MS Teams parses the body and replaces the entire credential key with it, dropping refresh_token and email. Lark, Webex, and Zoom feed the same response into handlers that require the provider envelope; a non-OK or invalid_grant-shaped sync error can mark the Zoom or Webex credential invalid. A hung sync URL blocks booking and availability indefinitely because fetch has no timeout.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zoho Bigin sync sends the credential id as the Cal.com user id

BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken passes credentialId, the Credential primary key, as the third argument of refreshOAuthTokens. That argument is posted as calcomUserId. Credential ids and user ids are independent sequences, so when sync is enabled the parent looks up tokens for the wrong person and can return another user's Zoho access token. The Bigin code then reads tokenInfo.data as if the result were an axios response. A Fetch Response has no .data, so refresh throws and Bigin calls fail. If the response parsing is fixed without fixing the id, the other user's token would be written onto this credential.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce always refreshes against production and then uses the old access token

getClient now always POSTs to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token and throws unless statusText is exactly "OK", before it builds the connection. Sandbox orgs must refresh at test.salesforce.com, and My Domain orgs use their own token URL; those refreshes fail and abort the client even when the stored access token is still valid. Previously a valid access token was used directly. The jsforce Connection is then created with credentialKey.access_token, the pre-refresh value, not the access token just returned, so an already-expired token is what this request uses. The refresh also ignores refreshOAuthTokens, so CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is never consulted for Salesforce. The value written back is accessTokenParsed.data; with sharing enabled that object has been reduced to access_token plus a fabricated refresh_token, so instance_url and the other Salesforce fields are dropped from the saved key.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook throws on bad input and stores decrypted keys with no shape check

The handler has no method check and no try/catch around zod parse, symmetricDecrypt, or JSON.parse. A non-POST, a missing body, a string userId (the schema is z.number(), not coerce), or a ciphertext that does not decrypt to JSON becomes an unhandled 500, and the crypto or parser message can be returned to the caller. The decrypted value is written straight into credential.key. An array, string, or unexpected object is accepted, so a buggy parent can persist a shape the app later casts and crashes on, with a 200 only if Prisma happens to accept it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Credential sync upsert is racy and can leave a stale duplicate

The webhook does findFirst({userId, appId}) and then either updates that id or creates a row. Those steps are not in a transaction, and Credential has no unique constraint on (userId, appId). The Lark callback in this PR already notes that userId and type are not unique, which is why that flow updates by credential id. Two concurrent deliveries, including a parent retry, can both see no row and both insert, or findFirst can update an arbitrary duplicate because there is no orderBy. Calendar code also uses findFirst, so it can keep using a stale credential while the webhook returns 200. A retried sync therefore does not reliably make the parent the source of truth.

Lark deletes the credential before the sync refresh can run

refreshAccessToken still deletes the credential and throws when the stored refresh token is missing or refresh_expires_date is expired. That check runs before the new refreshOAuthTokens call. With credential sync the parent is the source of truth, and the sync helper documents a response that only contains an access token and expiry, so the local refresh token may be absent or already expired. In that case Cal.com deletes the Lark row instead of asking CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT for a new access token. The connection is gone and later calendar calls fail until the user reconnects; a webhook replay cannot help if the row was removed and a later findFirst misses the replacement.

No tests for credential sync or the OAuth refresh persistence change

The diff adds a privileged webhook and changes token refresh for every major OAuth app, but there are no new tests, and the PR checklist says tests were not added. The manual plan only hits the webhook and a simulated sync refresh. A unit test that refreshes Google and Office 365 with sharing disabled and asserts the stored key is still the token object, with the previous refresh_token kept when the provider omits one, would have caught the universal credential corruption. The webhook also has no coverage for a wrong secret, a non-object decrypted payload, an invalid credential being cleared, or two concurrent creates.

Privileged credential webhook uses a raw reusable secret

This route can replace any user's integration credential, including calendar, video, CRM, and Stripe payment keys, for any app slug. The only check is inequality against a static header value. The compare is not constant-time, the secret is the raw header rather than an HMAC over the body, and there is no timestamp or nonce. A captured request stays valid forever and also discloses the secret itself, so the holder can forge new writes for every userId, not only replay one body. Rolling a rotated token back is enough to keep using a stolen OAuth refresh token after the parent thought it had replaced it.

Salesforce refresh calls prisma without importing it

The new getClient path calls prisma.credential.update, but this file never imports prisma. Every other adapter in the PR imports @calcom/prisma explicitly, so this is not a global. SalesforceCalendarService constructs this.conn by calling getClient, so the first Salesforce calendar operation throws ReferenceError before a jsforce connection is returned. Event create, update, delete, and contact sync fail for every Salesforce user as soon as this code runs, including deployments that never enable credential sync.

Synced credentials are not unmarked invalid

When a credential already exists, the webhook updates only key. It does not set invalid to false. Google, Webex, and Zoom in this PR set invalid true so a failed refresh stops being used. A parent that pushes a replacement token for a credential Cal.com already marked invalid still gets 200, but loaders that skip invalid rows will ignore the new keys and the integration stays disconnected.

Token sync request sends user id with no authentication

The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug. It does not send CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, an HMAC, or any other credential, and it does not require the URL to be https. That endpoint is expected to return OAuth access tokens. The parent app therefore cannot tell Cal.com from any other caller who can reach the URL, and a client that can reach it can request tokens for arbitrary user ids. An http:// endpoint value would also put bearer tokens on the wire in cleartext. Nothing in .env.example says the caller is unauthenticated. The response is trusted with no status check, so an error body can be stored as a credential.

Zoom sync asks for app slug zoomvideo but credentials are stored as zoom

Zoom's refresh calls refreshOAuthTokens with appSlug "zoomvideo", but the OAuth callback in this PR stores the credential with appId "zoom" and the install path uses slug "zoom". When credential sync is enabled, the parent is queried for zoomvideo and will not find the Zoom tokens it stored or received under zoom. Refresh fails and Zoom meetings cannot be created for synced users even when the webhook wrote a valid credential.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and racy

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but the filter uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) without lowercasing or trimming guest, and split(',') does not trim entries. Blocked@example.com bypasses blocked@example.com, and a space after a comma in the env var bypasses that entry. The same === comparison against existing attendees is case-sensitive, the input array is not deduped, and the organizer address is not excluded, so one request can createMany both a@x.com and A@x.com, the same address twice, or the host as their own guest. There is no unique (bookingId, email) constraint and the check-then-insert is not locked, so two concurrent calls can also insert the same guest twice. Duplicate rows break the attendee list and send duplicate invites. When every address is filtered, the error key emails_must_be_unique_valid is also used for blacklist hits, so the client shows 'Emails must be unique and valid' instead of a blocked-email error. If at least one address remains, dropped addresses are silent and the UI still toasts success.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner check requires both roles

isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. A membership has a single role, so this is either always false (if the helpers check ADMIN and OWNER exclusively) or true only for owners (if isTeamAdmin already treats OWNER as admin). Team admins who are not the booking host and not an attendee are rejected with FORBIDDEN, even though the flag is named and used as an admin-or-owner grant and the bookings UI treats team admins/owners as managers. They cannot add guests to team bookings they otherwise manage. This should be ||, and it should not query team id 0 when eventType.teamId is null.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Notifications use the raw address list and hide send failures

sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests array, not the filtered uniqueGuests that were actually inserted. In email-manager, newGuests.includes(attendee.email) is what chooses AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new ICS REQUEST) versus the guests-added notice. The dialog only receives bookingId, so a user can retype an existing attendee plus a new address; the existing attendee is skipped in the DB but still matches newGuests and gets a fresh booking-confirmation invite, which can duplicate the event on their calendar. evt.team is never set (the query does not even load eventType.team or hosts), so the team-member loop in sendAddGuestsEmails is dead and collective/round-robin co-hosts are not notified. Send failures are caught, logged as a fixed string without the error, and the mutation still returns success, so the UI shows 'Guests added' when nobody was emailed.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Add-guest emails ignore event-type email opt-out

Every other sender in this file checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail before sending. sendAddGuestsEmails does not take event-type metadata and always emails the organizer, every existing attendee, and each new guest, including full calendar invites. Event types with standard emails disabled still emit these messages when a guest is added. The handler has booking.eventType loaded and should pass its metadata so the same opt-out applies.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Attendee insert is not rolled back if calendar sync fails

prisma.booking.update createMany commits the new attendees before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, with no transaction and no compensating delete. If the calendar call throws (revoked credential, provider error, or the wrong user's credentials), the mutation fails but the rows remain. A retry then filters those emails out as already attending and throws BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the caller cannot finish calendar sync or notifications. The host sees an error while the booking already lists the guests, and the guests were never emailed because sendAddGuestsEmails runs only after the calendar call. Persist guests only after sync succeeds, or roll the insert back on failure.

Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the host's

EventManager is constructed from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), not from the booking host. The query already loads booking.user.credentials and never uses them. Calendar references on the booking are stored against the host credential. Attendees are explicitly allowed to call this mutation, and the team-owner branch is meant to allow non-hosts; those callers do not have the host credential, so updateCalendarAttendees cannot update the host event. It will throw (leaving the rows committed with no rollback) or skip. Either way the host calendar, and Meet/Zoom guest lists derived from it, do not gain the new guests. Build EventManager from the booking owner (and that user's calendar credentials), including co-host credentials for collective events.

Cancelled, past, and no-guest events still accept new guests

After the permission check the handler never reads booking status, endTime, or eventType.disableGuests before inserting attendees and emailing invites. Any logged-in attendee (not only the host) may call this with a numeric booking id. disableGuests is on the included event type and is ignored, so a host who turned guests off can still have arbitrary addresses emailed a CONFIRMED invite that includes the video URL and meeting password from the booking references. The same path runs for CANCELLED, REJECTED, and PENDING bookings, and for meetings that already ended. The new ICS builders hardcode status CONFIRMED. The bookings menu also offers this action for past confirmed rows (BookingListItem bookedActions, rendered around line 554), so this is not only a raw-API issue. Reject anything that is not an upcoming accepted booking, and honor disableGuests.

Guest list has no upper bound

guests is an unbounded z.array of emails, and MultiEmail can append fields without a cap. Any authenticated host or attendee can submit thousands of addresses in one call. The handler insert them and fans out a calendar invite per address containing the meeting URL. OrganizerAddGuestsEmail also puts every attendee email in replyTo, so a large list can exceed header limits and fail the send after the rows are already committed. Cap and dedupe the array in the schema before any writes or sends.

New guests are stored with an empty name

guestsFullDetails sets name to an empty string for every new guest. New guests are emailed via AttendeeScheduledEmail, which addresses them as `${name} <${email}>`, so the To header is ' <guest@example.com>'. Some mailers reject or blank that address, and calendar attendees are created with an empty display name. OrganizerAddGuestsEmail also interpolates attendees[0].name into the subject with no fallback (organizer-add-guests-email.ts line 28), so a blank first attendee yields 'with ' and no name. Store the email (or its local part) as the name when the guest did not provide one.

No tests for add-guests authorization or side effects

The new mutation ships with no handler or UI tests. Permission (admin vs owner vs attendee vs stranger), blacklist and case-variant duplicates, cancelled and seated bookings, the single-occurrence recurring case, and calendar or email failure after the insert are all untested, so the authorization, seat, and rollback bugs above would not be caught in CI.

One occurrence is updated but the event is marked recurring

The handler updates only the given bookingId, but evt.recurringEvent is set from booking.eventType.recurringEvent for every instance of a recurring type. That field is what scheduled emails and calendar updates use to treat a CalendarEvent as a series (RRULE / series update). The recurring tab hides this action, so it is used on a single upcoming occurrence, yet the invite and calendar payload still describe the whole series. A guest is then on every occurrence in Google/Outlook (or holds an RRULE invite) while only one Booking row lists them, so later instances disagree between Cal.com and the external calendar. Either omit recurringEvent and target that occurrence's calendar reference, or add the guest to every future booking in the recurringEventId group and update the series once.

Seated events are not capacity-checked and get no seat rows

createMany inserts plain Attendee rows and later copies seatsPerTimeSlot onto the calendar payload, but never compares current attendees plus new guests to seatsPerTimeSlot and never creates the per-attendee seat rows (reference UIDs) seated bookings use. Occupancy, the seats UI, and seat-scoped cancel/reschedule links will not include these people. Depending on whether availability counts attendees or seats, the slot is either overfilled with people who still have the meeting link, or marked full without usable seat records. Paid-per-seat events also skip payment for these extra people. Block this mutation when seatsPerTimeSlot is set, or add real seats through the seat booking path and enforce the cap.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount is a lost-update read-modify-write

Failures write retryCount to the value read at the start of the iteration plus one, instead of an atomic increment, and nothing claims the row (for example updateMany where id and scheduled false) before calling Twilio. This endpoint has no lock, and each reminder does several awaits, so a slow run overlaps the next cron tick. Both invocations can read the same retryCount, both call scheduleSMS, and both store the same next count. The new cap is then under-counted, so a reminder is attempted more than twice, and both runs can schedule a duplicate SMS. Use an atomic increment and a conditional update so a concurrent run cannot reset the counter or send twice.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount cleanup deletes reminders this job does not own

The new deleteMany ORs a bare retryCount > 1 predicate that is not limited to method SMS, scheduled false, or unsent rows. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP, and the comment above the query still claims it only removes past-dated SMS reminders. Any row whose retryCount exceeds 1 is hard-deleted, including future email/WhatsApp reminders and rows already marked scheduled that still store a Twilio referenceId. Today only this handler writes the column, so non-SMS rows stay at 0 unless another writer sets them, but a concurrent cron can already produce a bad row: both runs load the same unscheduled reminder, one sets scheduled true and referenceId after a successful scheduleSMS, and the other writes retryCount from the stale in-memory value without touching scheduled. The next run then deletes that live provider message, so booking cancellation can no longer look up the SID and stop it. Scope the predicate to unscheduled SMS reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Failed retry bookkeeping aborts the rest of the batch

The new catch block awaits workflowReminder.update and does not handle that update failing. Previously the catch only logged, so the loop always continued. If the update throws — the row was already removed by this cleanup in an overlapping run, the reminder disappeared mid-batch, or the DB blipped — the exception escapes the for-loop, the handler 500s, and every later reminder in the batch is left unscheduled. findMany has no orderBy, so which reminders sit behind the failing row is undefined, and a cron retry hits the same hole. The original scheduling error is also never logged when the bookkeeping update throws. Ignore a missing row (or otherwise guard the update) so one bookkeeping failure cannot stop the rest of the batch.

Two transient errors permanently wipe pending SMS reminders

Every exception in the per-reminder try, and every falsy scheduleSMS result, increments retryCount, and the next cron deletes all rows with retryCount > 1. That includes Twilio timeouts, rate limits, and failures while loading the organizer profile or rendering the template, not only permanent rejections such as an invalid number. There is no backoff, so two consecutive runs during a short provider or DB outage set retryCount to 2 on every unscheduled SMS reminder in the 7-day window. The following run's deleteMany removes all of them. Those reminders are not recreated, the delete is not logged per id, and attendees never get the SMS after the provider recovers. Only permanent send failures should count, or the limit needs backoff before rows are deleted.

Unsendable reminders never increment retryCount

retryCount is updated only when scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws. If there is no destination (SMS_NUMBER sendTo empty, or booking.smsReminderNumber null) or the rendered message is empty, the handler skips the row and leaves retryCount at 0. The earlier continue when workflowStep or booking is missing does the same. Those rows stay scheduled false with a future scheduledDate, so every cron run loads them again until scheduledDate is in the past. That is the unbounded reschedule loop this change is meant to stop, and a booking with no phone number never enters the Twilio path the new counter covers. Treat these terminal cases as failures, or delete them, so they are retired after the same limit.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
ANY() on a JS array is not a Postgres int array

In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, org and team authorization interpolate JavaScript number arrays into PostgreSQL ANY() at lines 164 (`"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})`), 168 (`"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})`), and 201 (`"userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})`). Prisma `$queryRaw` / `Prisma.sql` does not encode a JS array as a PostgreSQL `int[]`; the array is one untyped parameter, typically sent as text. PostgreSQL then fails the statement with an error such as `operator does not exist: integer = text` or `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side`. User scope only uses scalar binds, and the only test that executes SQL is user-scoped, so this is not caught. Team and org insights, the main authorization paths, will throw instead of returning bookings. Build the list with Prisma.join and an explicit cast, for example `"userId" = ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(userIds)}]::int[])`, and keep the empty-list guard because Prisma.join([]) is invalid SQL.

Unparenthesized OR fragment breaks caller AND filters

In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, getBaseConditions returns the authorization fragment as-is when there are no service filters (line 75). Team and org scope build that fragment as `(teamPredicate) OR (userPredicate)` with no parentheses around the whole OR (the reduce at lines 171-174 and 204-207). SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so the intended caller query `WHERE ${await service.getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= ${start} AND "startTime" < ${end}` is parsed as team-bookings OR (personal-bookings AND date window). Every matching team booking is returned regardless of the date filter, and any other AND predicate appended by the caller (status, member, and so on) is skipped on the team-booking branch. That over-returns rows, ignores the insights time window, and can defeat caller-side restrictions. The same shape exists on the event-type filter at line 106 (`eventTypeId = X OR eventParentId = X`) if getFilterConditions is embedded directly. The old Prisma `AND: [...]` where input did not have this trap, and getBaseConditions already parenthesizes when it combines auth and filters (line 73) but not when it returns auth alone. Wrap every returned fragment, including the OR reduce result, in parentheses so external AND/OR composition is safe.

toEqual on nested Prisma.sql fragments will fail

In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts, the team-scope assertion at line 295, the org-scope assertion at line 332, and the combined-filter assertion at line 429 expect `toEqual` against one flat `Prisma.sql` template. The service does not build those fragments as a single template: buildTeamAuthorizationCondition, buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, and buildFilterConditions nest fragments with `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR/AND (${condition})``. Prisma stores nested `Sql` objects in `values` and only flattens them when the query runs, so Vitest deep equality fails even when the rendered SQL matches. The PR notes these tests were not executed. User-scope and single-filter assertions can pass only because those paths return one uncomposed template. Compare a flattened statement, or assert on rows from an executed query, instead of `toEqual` on the `Sql` object; otherwise CI fails and the team/org SQL is never actually checked.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Empty updateMany throws after cache is written

fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache ends by calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Prisma Client rejects updateMany when data is an empty object (validation error: data needs at least one field), and updateMany does not apply @updatedAt anyway, so {} cannot bump the column. unwatchCalendar in this file calls fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache after deleting cache, and Google webhook/cron refresh uses the same method. Those flows now throw after CalendarCache rows have already been upserted, so a successful cache write is reported as a failure and retried. The new UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so this call does not serve the feature; remove it, or if the touch is required pass { updatedAt: new Date() } using UpdateManyMutationInput (the new repository method is typed as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which allows relation ops updateMany cannot apply).

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook helper writes the wrong .env and fails on Linux

ENV_FILE is the relative path "../.env", resolved from the process cwd rather than the script directory. Running ./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root (the usual invocation) creates or edits a .env outside the repository and never sets GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL where the app reads it; it can also modify an unrelated project's env file. The update on line 68 uses sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed on Linux errors and does not update the file. cleanup() then exits 0 even when URL extraction fails, so the failure is easy to miss.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache status treats expired rows as live cache

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache by credentialId and returns max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter. Availability reads (getCachedAvailability) ignore rows whose expiresAt is in the past, but those rows are not deleted. Any leftover expired row still yields a cacheUpdatedAt, and CredentialActionsDropdown treats a truthy cacheUpdatedAt as live cache. Google connections whose cache has expired still show "Last updated" and "Delete cached data" even though that cache is not served.

Delete cache leaves stale status in the UI

deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper loads that query with refetchOnWindowFocus: false and passes onChanged through as an optional prop, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old cacheUpdatedAt and the delete action. Users are told the cache was deleted while the page keeps offering to delete it until a full remount.

In-memory delegation calendars cannot see or delete cache

Cache status is loaded only via connectedCalendars.map(cal => cal.credentialId) and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. In-memory delegation credentials use negative credential IDs: calendar-cache.repository.ts treats credentialId < 0 as invalid for DB writes and reads those users' cache by userId plus key, not by the synthetic id. The status query therefore returns nothing for those connections, so the dropdown never shows cache. deleteCache.handler.ts (credential lookup where id = credentialId and userId = session user) also cannot find an in-memory delegation credential and throws "Credential not found or access denied". Org users on delegated Google Calendar cannot view or clear the cache this feature is meant to manage.

No tests for deleteCache ownership check

deleteCache is a new mutation that deletes every CalendarCache row for a credential after a single findFirst on id plus userId, and the PR adds no tests. Nothing asserts that another user's credentialId is rejected, that a missing credential deletes zero rows, or that a negative in-memory delegation id is denied. That where clause is the only authorization control; a regression would wipe another user's calendar cache without the suite catching it.

updatedAt backfill marks every existing cache as just written

The migration adds CalendarCache.updatedAt NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(). Every existing row, including stale or expired cache, receives the migration transaction time rather than when the cache value was actually written. The new UI displays that column as "Last updated", so after deploy every Google credential that has any CalendarCache row looks freshly synced until the next Prisma upsert. The leading comment is also wrong: it says the column is added without a default and cannot be applied to a non-empty table, but the SQL does add a default. Backfill from a real write time, or leave the column nullable so legacy rows show as unknown instead of a false timestamp.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cancel no longer awaits reminder cancellation

handleCancelBooking used to collect workflowReminder.deleteMany promises and await them with the other Prisma work. It now calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach and never awaits or collects those promises. The email helper only sets cancelled=true, which is the only signal the cron uses to stop SendGrid; the SMS helper cancels Twilio and deletes the row, and there is no SMS cron to finish that job. On serverless the runtime can freeze as soon as the handler returns, so those writes often never commit, the cron never sees the email as cancelled, and both email and SMS for the cancelled booking are still sent. Even when the write does commit, email cancellation is deferred to a 15-minute cron that only acts in the last hour, so a reminder due before the next tick is not stopped. Errors inside the managers are swallowed, and the handler still returns success.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete refills the 100-slot SendGrid cancel cap and fails open

When immediateDelete is true and a referenceId exists, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only POSTs /v3/user/scheduled_sends with status cancel and then returns. It does not delete the WorkflowReminder and does not set cancelled=true. SendGrid keeps that cancellation in scheduled_sends until the original sendAt (up to 72 hours), and this PR exists because that queue is capped at 100 pending cancellations account-wide; once it is full, further cancels fail and emails still go out. The hot callers pass true for every already-scheduled reminder regardless of how far away the send is: reschedule in handleNewBooking.ts (line 968), workflow deletion in workflows.tsx (line 214), and step deletion in workflows.tsx (line 521). A single workflow delete can therefore enqueue one long-lived cancel per upcoming reminder and trip the cap for the whole platform. If the POST fails, the catch only logs, cancelled is never set, and the cron will not retry, so the email is still delivered. On success the row is left looking active, so nothing records that the batch was already cancelled.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Cron cancel can miss, drop, or poison reminder cancellations

The new cancel pass does not reliably stop SendGrid sends for cancelled bookings. Before it runs, the handler deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder with scheduledDate <= now, including cancelled=true rows whose SendGrid send has not been cancelled yet. A cron invocation that starts at or after sendAt therefore destroys the only record that could still cancel the batch, and the email goes out. The new query only selects cancelled rows due within the next hour, and this job runs every 15 minutes, while SendGrid will not honor a cancel inside roughly the last 10 minutes before sendAt. A booking cancelled after the last successful tick (for example 10 minutes before the reminder) is not stopped, and the following run deletes the row instead of cancelling it. The loop at line 56 has no per-item try/catch and only awaits the Prisma deletes in Promise.all after every SendGrid call succeeds. Prisma deletes are lazy until awaited, so one failure (null referenceId, non-email referenceId, already-cancelled batch, or a reminder inside the 10-minute cutoff) skips those deletes.
