true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Success-path debug logs at Error level dump every cleaned ID

CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log at Error after every ID fetch and every delete (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579), including batches that find nothing. These are leftover debug statements: the fetch log's err is always nil because a real error already returned, and the messages fire on the normal success path. Error-level lines are what most Grafana deployments alert on, so every cleanup cycle will raise false errors for alert, dashboard, and API annotations plus orphaned tags. Each line also includes the full ID slice and the SQL condition. Batch size is configurable and the new test uses 32767, so a single line can be megabytes, flooding log pipelines and risking dropped real errors. Remove these calls, or at most log a count at Debug without the ID list.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same issue: debug logging statements are erroneously using the Error log level, which will pollute production error logs. Both suggest either removing them or lowering the log level to Debug.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cleanup interval accidentally reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute

Run() now ticks the background cleanup loop every 1 minute instead of every 10 minutes. Nothing in the PR description or the annotation deadlock fix calls for this, and it changes every job in this service (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, and annotations), not just annotation cleanup. clean() uses a 9-minute timeout that was paired with the 10-minute interval so one pass finished before the next tick. With a 1-minute ticker, any pass longer than a minute (likely now that each annotation batch is a separate SELECT plus DELETE, and on large tables) leaves a tick buffered, so the next pass starts immediately and cleanup runs back-to-back. That multiplies database load and can increase the write contention this change is meant to reduce. Restore the 10-minute interval unless a documented, intentional schedule change is actually wanted.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same change (cleanup ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute) and the same underlying concern (increased database load and contention).

false_positives.candidate:
SQLite IN-list is built with quadratic string concatenation

When the database is SQLite and AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is above 999, deleteByIDs inlines IDs by repeatedly assigning values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v). Each iteration copies the whole string, so n IDs cost O(n²) allocations before the DELETE is sent. The new test sets the batch size to 32767, and orphaned-tag cleanup can emit several lists of that size; that is on the order of gigabytes of temporary strings and multi-second stalls on the cleanup goroutine, which runs the other cleanup jobs only after annotations finish. Build the list with strings.Builder (and consider chunking) so large SQLite batches stay linear.

true_positives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Latencies are recorded on the wrong store's metric

On Storage.Create failure the code calls recordLegacyDuration (line 45) and never records a storage sample, so unified-storage create failures show up as legacy failures and storage error latency is missing. Update does the same on line 129 (recordLegacyDuration for a storage error). DeleteCollection's legacy goroutine calls recordStorageDuration (line 166) with the legacy start time, so legacy delete-collection latency and errors are added to the storage histogram and the legacy series stays empty. Dashboards and any mode-promotion checks that compare legacy vs storage success will attribute outages to the wrong store and can page or block migration incorrectly.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same bug where `recordStorageDuration` and `recordLegacyDuration` are swapped/incorrectly used in the `DeleteCollection` method (though the candidate describes it as the legacy goroutine calling `recordStorageDuration` and the golden comment has slightly garbled phrasing describing the mix-up between the two functions in `DeleteCollection`). The candidate also identifies similar mix-ups in `Create` and `Update`. They point to the exact same underlying metric recording bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Successful delete metrics use the object name as the kind label

The delete success path calls recordStorageDuration with name (the object name) as the third argument, while the error path two lines above and every other method pass options.Kind. That label is the resource kind. Every successful delete therefore emits a unique series per object name, which is unbounded cardinality on a hot write path and can exhaust Prometheus memory. Success and failure also cannot be aggregated together because they do not share the same label value, so delete success rate is not measurable.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same bug: passing `name` instead of `options.Kind` when recording metrics, which is inconsistent with other methods.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy writes are cancelled with the request context

Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection start the legacy write in a goroutine and derive its context with context.WithTimeoutCause on the incoming request context (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163). A child context is cancelled as soon as its parent is cancelled, and the apiserver cancels the request context when the handler returns — which is immediately after these methods return success. The 10s timeout therefore never keeps the legacy call alive; Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection run with an already-cancelled context and fail. Mode 3 reads only from unified storage, so the missed legacy write is invisible to API clients, but rollback to a legacy-read mode drops every write made in mode 3. The new playlist mode 3 integration tests that expect the legacy HTTP API to show k8s writes will fail or flake for the same reason.

Background legacy writes use the caller's objects without a copy

The legacy goroutines call Legacy.Create with the same obj pointer passed to Storage.Create (line 55), Legacy.Update with the same objInfo (line 139), and Legacy.DeleteCollection with the same listOptions (line 165). k8s create/update/delete-collection mutate those values in place (generated name, UID, resourceVersion, continue/resourceVersion on list options), and the caller may keep using them after the method returns. The goroutine therefore races with the storage layer and the client. Legacy create can also reject the object because resourceVersion/UID were already set by unified storage, or it can persist a different name than the one returned to the client. Deep-copy the inputs before the unified call (and clear server-assigned resourceVersion on the legacy copy) before handing them to the goroutine.

Legacy update no longer writes the object stored in unified storage

The previous Update loaded the unified object, ran objInfo.UpdatedObject once, and passed an updateWrapper so Legacy.Update received the exact object just written to unified storage. That wrapper is gone. Legacy.Update is now invoked with the original objInfo, so it loads the legacy row and re-runs UpdatedObject plus the client's preconditions against that row. Mode 3 serves reads from unified storage, so the resourceVersion on the update is the unified one and will not match legacy; a normal precondition check fails the legacy update with a conflict and the backup copy is never updated. Even if legacy ignores resourceVersion, a patch is applied to drifted legacy state instead of replacing it with the unified result, so the stores diverge. Delete has the same precondition problem: line 112 forwards the caller's DeleteOptions, including a unified-storage resourceVersion precondition, into Legacy.Delete.

Unified NotFound skips the legacy delete

Delete returns immediately on any Storage.Delete error, including NotFound, and never starts the legacy delete. The previous implementation still deleted from legacy when unified storage returned NotFound, and only treated other errors as fatal. After a failed or cancelled legacy delete, a retry sees NotFound in unified storage (the source of truth for reads) and now leaves the legacy object in place permanently. Orphans also remain for objects that exist only in legacy. NotFound should still be returned to the client, but the async legacy delete should run so the backup store is cleaned up.

Legacy write failures are not logged

The goroutines in Create (line 56), Delete (line 113), Update (line 140), and DeleteCollection (line 166) only feed the legacy error into a duration metric and otherwise discard it. The previous synchronous implementation logged legacy create/update/delete/delete-collection failures. With writes now best-effort and easy to cancel, a broken legacy path produces no log line, so operators cannot tell which object diverged or why (conflict, timeout, cancelled context, validation). Log errObjectSt/err with the object name before recording the metric.

Expected NotFound responses are logged as errors

Get logs every Storage.Get error at Error level, including NotFound (line 71). List (line 87) and Delete (line 102) do the same, and the apierrors.IsNotFound guard that the old Delete used was removed. NotFound on get/delete is a normal client result (the playlist tests even delete twice and expect it). Those calls will flood error logs and hide real storage failures. Log NotFound at a higher verbosity, or not at all, and keep Error for unexpected failures.

Destroy does not wait for in-flight legacy writes

Destroy closes Storage and then Legacy immediately and does not track the goroutines started by Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection. Those goroutines can still be inside Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection after Legacy.Destroy returns, which races with teardown and can panic or hit a closed database. Shutdown also drops the backup writes the goroutines were supposed to finish. A WaitGroup (or similar) should be added around the legacy goroutines and waited on in Destroy before calling Legacy.Destroy.

Unit tests never check that the legacy write happens

Mode 3 success tests register legacy mock expectations but return as soon as the unified call finishes (Create at line 65, and the same pattern in Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection) and never call AssertExpectations or wait for the goroutine. The defining behavior — an asynchronous legacy write — is therefore untested, and a cancelled or skipped legacy call still passes. Legacy and unified also share one testify mock, so method names like Create cannot be attributed to a store; the "unified store fails" create case only stubs the legacy Create expectation, which the synchronous storage call consumes by accident. testify mocks are not thread-safe, so the background call can also race or panic after the test function returns.

Mode 3 playlist tests assume legacy is updated before the handler returns

The new mode 3 cases (file at line 132, unified storage at line 191, etcd at line 287) reuse doPlaylistTests. That helper creates, updates, and deletes through the k8s client and then immediately requires the legacy /api/playlists API to match (search at line 529 and getFromBothAPIs). Mode 3 returns after the unified write and only then writes legacy on another goroutine whose context is tied to the request. The legacy HTTP read therefore races the backup write and, because that context is cancelled when the request ends, will often never see the object. These new integration cases will fail or flake until the test waits for the legacy write or the dual writer detaches that work from request cancellation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

true_positives.golden_comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Filtered Grafana rows are rendered without React keys

FilterViewResults builds a KeyedRuleWithOrigin key specifically to avoid duplicate list keys, and the previous GrafanaRuleLoader was rendered with key={key}. The replacement GrafanaRuleListItem omits that prop, while the datasource and unknown branches in the same map still set key. Grafana rows are therefore unkeyed siblings of keyed rows. As infinite scroll appends pages, React can reuse the wrong row instance (open More menu or silence-drawer state) and will warn about missing keys. getGrafanaRuleKey on line 209 also has a stray closing brace (`rule.uid}}`), so putting key={key} back without fixing that helper still yields malformed keys.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: the `GrafanaRuleListItem` component rendered inside a list is missing the required React `key` prop, which can lead to rendering issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Silence menu item does nothing without a ruler rule

The list menu shows Silence notifications because useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities allows it for Grafana alerting rules, and handleSilence only sets showSilenceDrawer. The drawer is mounted only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true, where rule is the optional ruler-rule prop. GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule, so that condition is false and the click is a no-op. SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer still requires a RulerGrafanaRuleDTO; the list needs a fetch-on-demand or a drawer that can create the silence from the prom rule uid and labels. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test only asserts the menu item is present and never clicks it.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue describe the exact same bug: in list views (like GrafanaRuleListItem), only `promRule` is passed to `RuleActionsButtons` without `rule` (the ruler rule). While the 'Silence notifications' menu item is now shown based on promRule abilities, clicking it only sets `showSilenceDrawer` without actually rendering `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` because the drawer still requires the ruler `rule` prop to be present.

false_positives.candidate:
skipToken still grants Grafana Duplicate on non-Grafana rules

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is called with skipToken (converted to undefined) whenever the menu has no Grafana Prometheus rule, including every datasource-managed rule. useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(undefined) returns loading:false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported, and Duplicate is then [true, user has Grafana AlertingRuleCreate] via toAbility(getRulesPermissions('grafana').create). AlertRuleMenu ORs that tuple with the ruler ability (canDuplicate), so an editor who may create Grafana-managed rules but may not write external rules still sees Duplicate and the clone flow is started with the cloud rule identifier. skipToken is meant to skip the check, but it does not return [false, false]. View and Explore are the same shape (supported plus a global permission even when the rule is missing) and will leak if callers OR them the same way. Existing RBAC tests mock these hooks, so they never execute this path.

Delete stays hidden in the list view without a ruler rule

The new list passes only a Prometheus rule into RuleActionsButtons, and AlertRuleMenu now treats the Grafana prom-rule delete ability as enough for canDelete. The Delete item is still rendered only when rulerRule is truthy (canDelete && rulerRule) and the click passes that ruler rule into handleDelete. The list no longer loads ruler rules, so rulerRule is undefined and Delete never appears, even for users with folder delete permission. RuleActionsButtons already ignores the ruler argument and calls showDeleteModal with the uid identifier built from the prom rule, so the gate is leftover and removes an action that would otherwise work.

Pause is unreachable once ruler rules are dropped from the list

canPause is now true for an editable Grafana alerting rule based on useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, but the Pause item is still rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) is true, and it passes that ruler rule into MenuItemPauseRule. GrafanaRuleListItem never supplies a ruler rule, so Pause cannot appear in the list the PR is migrating. Dropping the rulerRule check is not sufficient: MenuItemPauseRule still requires a RulerGrafanaRuleDTO. The prom rule already has uid and isPaused, but nothing maps those into the pause action, and onPauseChange is not wired from RuleActionsButtons either.

Federated rule groups are no longer immutable

useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to set isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) (true when the group has source_tenants) and treat those rules as immutable. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated to false and drops the isFederatedRuleGroup import. useAlertRuleAbility still goes through this for every CombinedRule, not only the new list. Update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent delete therefore become supported for federated Mimir/GEM groups whenever the user otherwise has permission. Editing those rules through the normal form rewrites the ruler group and can strip source_tenants, breaking cross-tenant evaluation.

Recording rules lose export and pause in prom-rule abilities

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities uses isAlertingRule (Prometheus alerting type only) as the support flag for ModifyExport, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently. The ruler ability path uses isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which is true for both Grafana alerting and recording rules, and the comment here says every GrafanaPromRuleDTO is Grafana-managed by definition. Recording rules in the new list therefore lose Export, and Pause stays unsupported even after the rulerRule menu gate is fixed. Silence correctly depends on alerting type; these other actions should not. Detail views that still use ruler abilities will keep showing Export and Pause for the same recording rule, so the two UIs disagree.

Rule view links drop the returnTo back-navigation target

The removed list item built the view href with createReturnTo() so the rule detail back link returned to the current list URL, including search filters. The new GrafanaRuleListItem always links to `/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view` with no returnTo query param. Opening a rule from the group list or the filtered list therefore loses that context, and back navigation no longer returns to the same filtered results. Group-loader tests only assert that the href contains the view path, so they do not catch the missing parameter.

Menu test asserts the incomplete action set

The new More-menu test grants AlertingRuleUpdate and AlertingRuleDelete, defines a Delete menuitem selector, and then asserts the menu contains exactly four items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export). That locks in the missing Delete and Pause actions introduced by dropping ruler rules. It also never clicks Silence, so it does not notice that the drawer does not open. A green run of this file does not cover the list-view action regressions, and RulesTable RBAC tests mock useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities entirely, so they do not execute the skipToken permission logic either.

$__range queries are split after early interpolation

runSplitQuery now passes every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before querySupportsSplitting. applyTemplateVariables interpolates with TemplateSrv.replace, and during dashboard or Explore queries that replaces $__range, $__range_s, and $__range_ms from the active time range. querySupportsSplitting then calls isQueryWithRangeVariable on that already-substituted expr, so the macro is gone and the query is treated as splittable. The comment on querySupportsSplitting says these queries must not be split: the backend fills $__range from the time range of the request it actually receives, and a split chunk is not the range the user selected. After this change, rate({job="app"}[$__range]) over several days is rewritten to a fixed full-window duration (for example [7d]) and then executed as one-day chunks, each looking back the whole window. Merged results do not match an unsplit query. The new tests cannot catch this: they stub replace to rewrite only $__auto and $step, so $__range stays in the expression under test and the guard still looks like it works. Check isQueryWithRangeVariable on the raw expr and keep those targets in the non-splitting partition before interpolating.

Shard path applies template variables twice

runShardSplitQuery already maps each target through applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) before sharding. For every shard group it then calls runSplitQuery with a sub-request that still carries request.filters and the already interpolated targets, and runSplitQuery maps those targets through applyTemplateVariables again. Substitution is not idempotent: the first pass turns an escaped $$ into a literal $, and the second pass treats that $ as a variable, so a label value or query text containing $name can be expanded to a different variable. Ad hoc filters are applied on both passes (the old interpolateVariablesInQueries call did not receive request.filters; both new call sites do), so matchers are inserted once before the shard selector is injected and again after. The executed LogQL ends up with duplicate label matchers, for example {job="x", env="prod", __stream_shard__=~"1|2", env="prod"}. The shard test now expects applyTemplateVariables five times (once up front plus once per shard group), which locks in the double pass instead of interpolating once.

Expressions that interpolate to empty hang shard splitting

runShardSplitQuery used to interpolate with interpolateVariablesInQueries and then drop targets with an empty expr. It now filters on the raw expr and only then calls applyTemplateVariables. A target whose whole expression is a variable, such as $query, passes the filter because the raw string is non-empty, then becomes expr: '' after substitution, and is still passed to splitQueriesByStreamShard. If that target is alone in a group (non-shardable groups are queued first, so one empty query next to shardable queries is enough), runNextRequest calls runSplitQuery, which filters the empty expr out and calls runSplitGroupedQueries with an empty request list. That function immediately evaluates requests.filter(...)[0].partition and throws TypeError. The throw is inside a .then() with no rejection handler, so the subscriber never errors or completes and the whole request hangs, including valid sibling queries. Previously the empty target was removed before grouping and the other queries ran. The same filter-before-map in runSplitQuery (line 298) also keeps an empty interpolated expr in a split group and sends it to runQuery, which fails the batch with a Loki parse error.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Device limit check and insert are not atomic

When device_limit is positive, CreateOrUpdateDevice counts rows in one WithDbSession and, if the count is under the limit, inserts in a second WithDbSession. Nothing wraps the two statements in a transaction or takes a lock, and the unique key is only on device_id, so it does not cap the number of rows. Concurrent anonymous requests that all observe count < limit will all insert. With 50 simultaneous new device ids and a limit of 10, all 50 can commit and the table stays at 50; nothing rolls the extras back. That is the multi-instance, multi-user load this cap is meant to control, so AnonymousDeviceLimit is not a hard limit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the exact same race condition where concurrent requests check the device count and insert new devices without a wrapping transaction or lock, allowing the device limit to be exceeded.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer takes an anonstore.AnonStore and now requires db.DB, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained a bare int64 device-limit argument. The new test runs on SQLite only, so MySQL/Postgres placeholder or rows-affected differences in the new UPDATE are not exercised.

The code treats 0 as 'do not enforce' rather than 'allow zero devices', and that is not stated anywhere a user will see it. true_positives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Add/remove failures are silent and desync the pager

addMembers and removeMember (line 56) ignore the promises returned by the model. Those model methods only call findMembers on success and have no failure path. save and destroy in this same controller show a bootbox alert. A 400, 422 from an automatic group, or 500 therefore leaves the list unchanged with no message, so the admin cannot tell a failure from a no-op. next and previous also write offset before findMembers resolves, so a failed page load leaves the pager on a page whose members were never fetched. Overlapping findMembers responses are applied unconditionally, so a slower earlier page can overwrite a newer one.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment points out that findMembers() is now asynchronous and its returned promise is unhandled, leading to race conditions and member data not being immediately available. While the candidate issue primarily frames the title around silent failures, it explicitly identifies the unhandled asynchronous nature of findMembers() causing state desync and race conditions ('next and previous also write offset before findMembers resolves... Overlapping findMembers responses are applied unconditionally, so a slower earlier page can overwrite a newer one'). Both identify the same underlying bug regarding unhandled async findMembers calls and resulting race conditions.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

totalPages is one too high when count divides evenly

totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is a positive multiple of limit (50, 100, and so on) that is an extra page: 50 members with limit 50 displays 1/2 and leaves Next enabled. next() then sets offset to user_count, findMembers returns no rows, and the admin lands on a blank member page. Math.ceil(user_count / limit) is the right count (0 stays 0).
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the exact same pagination off-by-one bug where user_count being a multiple of limit (e.g., total == limit) allows navigating via next() to an offset equal to user_count, displaying page 2/2 with no members.

true_positives.golden_comment: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Add/remove members require group_id the route never sets

add_members and remove_member (line 85) load the group with params.require(:group_id). The new routes in config/routes.rb are bare put/delete "members" inside resources :groups, which are member routes on /admin/groups/:id/members. That segment is params[:id], the same param this controller already uses for update and destroy. Elsewhere in routes.rb a non-default name is written into the path (delete "groups/:group_id"); these member routes do not do that, so group_id is never populated. The Ember client only interpolates the id into the path and posts usernames or user_id, not group_id. require(:group_id) raises ParameterMissing and every add or remove returns 400. Controller specs stay green because they pass group_id directly and never hit the router. Read params[:id], matching update/destroy.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: the controller actions attempt to read `params[:group_id]` instead of `params[:id]`, which is what the route actually provides, causing group membership actions to fail.

false_positives.candidate:
Members action requires group_id but the route sets id

The rewritten members action still calls find_group(:group_id), and find_group does params.require on that key. The route is get "members" inside resources :groups, i.e. GET /groups/:id/members, so the group name arrives in params[:id]. show in this same controller correctly uses find_group(:id); posts and counts have the same mismatch. Group#findMembers requests /groups/:name/members.json and only sends limit and offset, not group_id. The action 400s before it can return the new members/meta payload, so both the admin member list and the public members page stay empty. Use find_group(:id).

remove_member passes an integer to association delete

remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) with a raw integer. On Rails 4, CollectionAssociation#delete type-checks its arguments and raises ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch (User expected, got Fixnum) instead of deleting the group_users join row. Once the group_id param bug is fixed, removing a member still 500s and the user stays in the group. The new spec expects 200 and a user count of 0, so it fails if run. Load the user and call group.remove(user), which is what the previous membership update path used, or pass a User record to delete.

Public members page cannot show past the first 50 users

The public members route only calls model.findMembers() once, and Group#findMembers always sends limit 50 (the model default). groups/members.hbs has no pager and does not show the new meta.total. GroupsController#members now applies that limit to every group. Previously non-automatic groups returned every member and automatic groups defaulted to 200. Anyone opening a group with more than 50 members sees a silently truncated list and has no way to load the rest. The admin screen has next/previous; this page does not. Either paginate here or request a limit large enough to preserve the old full list.

Create ignores alias_level the form submits

create sets name and visible but never alias_level. The new-group form shows the alias-level combo outside the id check, and Group#asJSON posts alias_level on create. The column stays at the default 0 (nobody can mention the group). The client only copies resp.basic_group.id back onto the model, so the UI keeps the level the admin chose and then transitions to the group page. They have no reason to hit Save again; after a reload the mention permission has reverted. update does persist alias_level. The create spec only checks that the name is stripped.

Member reloads use the unsaved group name

findMembers requests /groups/ plus this.get('name') plus /members.json. In the admin form the name text field is two-way bound to that same property, and pagination, add, and remove all call findMembers before Save. An edited but unsaved name is sent to the server. If it matches no group the reload 404s and the member list fails with no error UI (next/previous have already moved offset). If it matches a different group, that group's members are shown on this group's screen while add/remove still target this group's numeric id, so the admin can change the wrong memberships. Fetch with the persisted name, not the in-progress field.

Enter in the group form activates Add instead of Save

The admin group editor is now wrapped in a form, but Add, Save, and Delete are button elements with no type attribute, so they default to submit. On an existing non-automatic group the first submit button is Add. Pressing Enter in the name field (or the user selector) activates Add rather than Save: members are added, or addMembers returns immediately because the username box is empty, and the name, visibility, and alias level are not saved. Delete is also a submit button. Set type="button" on these action buttons. If the action helper does not preventDefault, the browser will also GET-submit the form to the current URL and reload the page, dropping unsaved edits.

Spaced usernames are skipped and add still succeeds

add_members splits the usernames string on commas and calls User.find_by_username on each token without stripping. A space after a comma, which is normal when typing into the selector ("alice, bob"), does not match username_lower, so that user is not added. Unknown names are skipped the same way. If group.save then succeeds, the action still renders success_json even when nobody was added. The admin UI reloads the current page and does not clear the input (the controller has a TODO for that), so the add looks successful. Strip each username and report names that did not match instead of returning success unconditionally.

Members limit and offset are unbounded

limit and offset come from the query string with only to_i and no range check. The endpoint is available to anyone who can see the group. limit=1000000 loads and serializes every member of a large automatic group such as trust_level_0 in one response, which is a straightforward DoS. offset=-1 or limit=-1 makes PostgreSQL reject the statement (OFFSET/LIMIT must not be negative) and the action returns 500. Clamp offset to >= 0 and cap limit to a small maximum; the UI only requests 50.

Members JSON shape and default size break existing clients

GET /groups/:name/members.json used to return a top-level JSON array of users (the previous client called result.map on it). It now returns an object with members and meta. When limit is omitted the action also returns at most 50 rows instead of the full roster for custom groups or the previous default of 200 for automatic groups. In-repo callers in this PR were updated, but external API clients, scripts, and plugins that still expect an array will throw or stop listing members, and callers that omitted limit silently lose everyone past 50. There is no version flag or fallback to the old shape.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Match stats are written during validation and counted twice per signup

EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block? from validate_each, but should_block? is not a pure check: on any hit it increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and save the row, including when action_type is do_nothing (the method returns false and no error is added). UsersController#create calls user.valid? at line 168 and then user.save at line 172, and save runs validations again. One signup attempt against a screened address therefore records two matches. The same write runs for every other valid? or failed save, including attempts that never create a user. match_count and last_match_at, which the model spec treats as the record of how often an address was seen, will be inflated, and every anonymous signup POST that hits a screened address performs a database write as a side effect of validation. Record the match once, after a real attempt, with an atomic update outside the validator.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same core issue: the `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (or `should_block_email?`) predicate method is not a pure read check because it has the side effect of updating database statistics (match_count and last_match_at). The candidate provides additional concrete examples of how this side effect causes bugs during validation (e.g., double counting on valid? and save).

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain allow/deny regexp is unanchored and barely escaped

email_in_restriction_setting? interpolates the site setting into a regexp of the form @(domain-list) after escaping only dots, then matches with =~, which succeeds on any substring and is not anchored at the end of the address. A whitelist entry of company.com therefore accepts attacker@company.com.evil.com. A blacklist entry of spam.com does not match user@mail.spam.com, because the character before spam.com is a dot rather than @, so subdomain addresses bypass the blacklist. Other regexp metacharacters in the setting are not escaped, so an invalid fragment raises RegexpError during validation and registration returns 500 instead of a validation error. This is the domain check moved from User, and it is still wrong. Anchor the host to the end of the string, decide explicitly whether subdomains should match, and escape metacharacters before interpolation.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same vulnerability in the `email_in_restriction_setting?` method: the regex `@(#{domains})` lacks proper boundary anchoring, allowing domain restriction bypasses via subdomains or appended domains.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email match is case-sensitive and does not trim

BlockedEmail.should_block? loads a row with an exact where(email: email) comparison, and nothing downcases or strips the address on write or lookup. Uniqueness is case-sensitive, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive, so User@spam.com and user@spam.com can both be stored and only one of them matches. Signup assigns params[:email] unchanged (User.new_from_params) and EmailValidator passes that raw value in. Elsewhere this app treats addresses as case-insensitive: UsersController#change_email uses Email.downcase(...).strip, and the domain regexp is built ignore-case. A listed address can therefore be used to register by changing case or adding surrounding whitespace, so the block list does not stop the signup it is meant to stop. Normalize with the same downcase-and-strip helper on save and in should_block?, and enforce a case-insensitive unique index.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue directly identifies the same problem as the golden comment: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a case-sensitive email lookup, which allows bypassing the blocklist by changing the case of the email address.

false_positives.candidate:
match_count update is a lost-update read-modify-write

should_block? loads match_count, adds 1 in Ruby, and save writes that absolute value back. Two concurrent requests that both read the same count will both persist count+1, so attempts are dropped. save also runs validations and callbacks and writes every dirty column, so a failure or delay on this row can turn a signup validation into an error, or overwrite a concurrent last_match_at. Increment with an atomic update (update_counters or increment_counter) and set last_match_at with update_column so concurrent matches are not lost and other columns are not rewritten.

Specs miss case bypass, double-count, and domain rules

EmailValidator specs stub BlockedEmail.should_block? and never create a blocked row, and BlockedEmail specs only call should_block? with the exact stored string. Nothing asserts that User validation (validates :email, email: true) rejects a blocked address, that a case or whitespace variant is blocked, that UsersController#create increments match_count once, or that the whitelist/blacklist branches accept or reject the suffix and subdomain cases above. Those bugs would leave this suite green.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items() mixin emits an invalid property and skips old Firefox

align-items() copies one keyword into every prefix and emits -ms-align-items, which is not a CSS property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, already set above). Old Firefox, which flexbox() and inline-flex() target with display: -moz-box and display: -moz-inline-box, needs -moz-box-align, and that declaration is missing. Header .contents, .small-action, and .badge-wrapper.bullet therefore become 2009 boxes with no cross-axis alignment in that engine, so the vertical centering and bullet baseline alignment this PR adds do not apply. The 2009 and IE10 properties also do not accept modern keywords: flex-start and flex-end must be mapped to start and end for -webkit-box-align, -moz-box-align, and -ms-flex-align, while -webkit-align-items and align-items keep the modern names. center and baseline happen to be valid in all three syntaxes, so IE10 and old WebKit align for the current call sites, but the mixin is wrong for the other standard values.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly identifies the exact same problem described in the golden comment: that `-ms-align-items` is not a valid CSS property and that IE uses `-ms-flex-align` instead. It also includes additional context about other browser prefixes in the same mixin, which encompasses the core issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin is off by one for 2009 box-ordinal-group

order() writes $val straight through to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (initial value 1, legal values are integers >= 1); standard order is 0-based (initial value 0). The matching prefix is $val + 1. As written, order(0) emits box-ordinal-group: 0, which is invalid and dropped so the item stays in the default group; order(1) ties with unordered siblings instead of following them; a negative order, the usual way to pull an item to the front, is invalid and ignored. -ms-flex-order and -webkit-order correctly share order's numbering, so IE10 and 2012-spec WebKit are fine. Header callers pass 2 and 3, which still sort after default items in both systems, but the mixin does not implement order for any other value. Add 1 on the two box-ordinal-group declarations.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based properties (requiring values >= 1), whereas standard `order` is 0-based, so passing `$val` (especially 0) directly to them causes invalid/incorrect rendering.

false_positives.candidate:
Flexbox on .small-action unpins the action button and shrink-wraps the description

.small-action is now a flex container (display:flex via the new flexbox mixin, align-items:center), and .small-action-desc is no longer a full-width block. Its padding changed from 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em to 0 1.5%, and it has no flex-grow, so it shrink-wraps to its text. The staff delete/recover control is positioned only by .small-action button { float: right }, which used to pin it to the right edge of that full-width row. Float does not apply to flex items, so a button that is a direct child stays in source order beside the label; a button nested in .small-action-desc only floats to the right of the shrink-wrapped description, not the post row. On short actions the control sits against or over the label instead of at the far right. Set flex: 1 and min-width: 0 on .small-action-desc so an inner float can still reach the row edge, or drop the float and push the button with margin-left: auto.

Header panel is not pinned right in the 2009 flexbox the new mixin enables

.d-header .panel no longer has float: right, and .d-header .title no longer has float: left. The replacement is margin-left: auto on .panel inside a .contents flex container, plus order. Auto margins absorb free space in modern flexbox and in IE10 (-ms-flexbox), so current Chrome, Firefox, Safari 7+, and IE10 still pin the icons to the right. They do not in the 2009 model: display: -webkit-box and display: -moz-box, which the new flexbox() mixin emits, treat auto margins as 0 and only distribute space with box-flex / -webkit-box-flex, which is never set. Browsers that only understand those prefixes (Safari 6, iOS 6, Android 4.3 stock browser, Firefox 21 and older) pack the logo, topic info, and controls on the left instead of keeping the menu at the right edge. Browsers with no flexbox at all lose the float fallback and stack the logo and panel as normal blocks. Keep float: left / float: right as the non-flex fallback (a flex formatting context ignores float on the items) and drop the 2009 display values, or add a 2009 pack so those prefixes actually reproduce the header.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is never called

ActiveModel::Serializers includes an attribute only if include_<name>? returns true. Every other hook in this serializer uses that form (include_email?, include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, and the methods defined by untrusted_attributes). include_website_name has no question mark, so it is never invoked and the website.present? guard is dead code. website_name is therefore always serialized, including a null website_name when the user has no website or the host cannot be parsed. The omission the new method was written to provide cannot happen.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue accurately identifies the primary bug described in the golden comment: the `include_website_name` method is missing the required `?` suffix needed by ActiveModel::Serializers to conditionally include attributes. Although the golden comment also mentions a secondary issue regarding string literal mutation (`'.' << website_host`), the core defect is matched with high precision.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-domain check mismatches common hosts

The decision to append the URL path does not compare registrable domains, so it both over-matches and under-matches. The elsif treats hosts as the same site when they have the same label count greater than 2 and share every label after the first. That equates unrelated sites that only share a public suffix: a forum at forum.co.uk and a website of http://phishing.co.uk/login both reduce to co.uk, so the profile shows phishing.co.uk/login instead of phishing.co.uk. The same false positive applies to *.com.au, *.co.jp, *.blogspot.com, *.github.io, and similar. The else branch only checks discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host), so the path is added when the website is a parent of the forum, but not when the website is a subdomain of the forum. A forum at example.com with website http://www.example.com/docs or http://blog.example.com/users/jane displays only www.example.com or blog.example.com, which hides the path this change is meant to show. Comparison is also case-sensitive: URI#host is lowercased, but Discourse.current_hostname is not normalized here, so a mixed-case hostname fails the exact-match branch and drops the path. The new specs only cover an unrelated host, an exact match, and the website-is-parent direction; they never exercise the elsif or the www/subdomain cases.

Non-ASCII website URLs vanish from the profile

The host is parsed with URI(...).host rescue nil, and a nil host makes website_name return nil. The profile template now shows the globe and link only when model.website_name is present, with no fallback to model.website. Ruby's stdlib URI raises URI::InvalidURIError on non-ASCII input (for example http://例え.jp/path) and on URLs containing spaces; those errors are swallowed, so website_name is null and the link disappears even though website is still stored and is still serialized for viewers allowed to see it. The old client label used website.split("/")[2], which still displayed a hostname for those strings. Internationalized profile websites that previously appeared are now omitted until rewritten as ASCII or punycode.

Website label goes stale after website changes

The header used to label the site with a controller computed property that observed model.website and updated when the website changed. It now renders the server field model.website_name, which is copied onto the model only when the user payload is first loaded. User#save sends the new website but only copies bio_excerpt back from the PUT response, so it never refreshes website_name. The header lives in user.hbs outside {{outlet}} and stays visible on preferences and other child routes. After model.website changes, the anchor href is the new URL while the link text is still the previous website_name until a full reload, so the visible label can name a different host than the link destination.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check is an inverted substring test

postMessageReceived accepts the event when discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is not -1, i.e. when the configured URL string contains the sender origin. That is the opposite of an origin allowlist and also ignores e.source, so it is not limited to this iframe. Any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl is treated as trusted. If discourseUrl is http://forum.example.com:3000/, a page at http://forum.example.com (port 80) matches at index 0 and can set iframe.height. Compare parsed origins for equality and require e.source === iframe.contentWindow. The same file concatenates discourseUrl + "embed/best" with no slash normalization (line 7), so a discourseUrl without a trailing slash requests a non-existent host path and the embed 404s.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same vulnerability: the origin validation in postMessage uses `indexOf`, which is an insufficient substring check that can be bypassed by unauthorized origins.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Spoofable Referer is enough to fetch URLs and create topics

best enqueues retrieve_topic for any embed_url when the Referer host matches embeddable_host. Referer is fully client-controlled, the route is an unauthenticated GET, and TopicRetriever only compares URI(embed_url).host to that setting (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15). It does not restrict scheme beyond what open accepts, port, path, or redirects. import_remote then calls open(url).read (topic_embed.rb:48). open-uri follows redirects to other hosts by default, so an open redirect on the embeddable host (or a 302 to link-local/metadata addresses) becomes server-side request forgery, including port probes such as http://embeddable-host:6379/. The 60s throttle key is per URL, so an attacker can enqueue a distinct job and create a distinct public topic for every query string that returns HTTP 200, all as embed_by_username, bypassing SpamRulesEnforcer because import passes skip_validations. There is no body size limit or timeout, so this is also a memory/job-queue DoS. Require a non-spoofable control (signed embed token), re-validate every redirect hop against an allowlist, cap response size, and rate-limit imports globally.

The embed view prints it with raw post.cooked (best.html.erb:19), and the normal topic page also treats cooked as HTML, so the payload runs on the Discourse origin for every viewer. The URL is attacker-controlled: /embed/best only checks a spoofable Referer host, then the retrieve job accepts any http(s) URL whose host equals embeddable_host. true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

There is no per-item rescue, and the job sets sidekiq retry: false, so one such item aborts the rest of the feed and the same crash repeats every hour. String#scrub also does not exist before Ruby 2.1, so this line fails even when content is present on 1.9/2.0. true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Referer is interpolated into a script string (reflected XSS)

The embed layout writes request.referer into a single-quoted JavaScript string with <%= %>. On Rails 3.2 and 4.0 that helper escapes &, <, >, and double quotes, but not single quotes, and it is not a JavaScript escape. ensure_embeddable only checks that URI(referer).host equals SiteSetting.embeddable_host, and Ruby's URI parser allows ' and () in the query. A parent URL such as http://eviltrout.com/?x=';alert(document.domain);// therefore passes the host check and is rendered as parent.postMessage(..., 'http://eviltrout.com/?x=';alert(document.domain);//'); which runs in the Discourse origin. This layout wraps both the loading and best responses, and a normal blog page that includes the embed script sends the full parent URL (including query string) as Referer. Any logged-in user who opens a crafted link on the embeddable host executes attacker script in the iframe and can perform forum actions as that user. true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same reflected XSS vulnerability caused by interpolating `request.referer` directly into a JavaScript string without proper JavaScript escaping.

false_positives.candidate:
import_remote uses Kernel#open without requiring open-uri

import_remote fetches the article with open(url).read but never requires open-uri. Kernel#open only treats the argument as an HTTP URL after open-uri is loaded; otherwise it opens a local path and raises Errno::ENOENT, so no topic is created. poll_feed.rb requires open-uri at load time, and TopicRetriever calls PollFeed before fetch_http only when feed polling is enabled, so on-demand import accidentally depends on that file having been loaded in-process. The Disqus thor task calls import_remote without requiring open-uri either. The call also has no read timeout or byte limit, and a nil doc.content then crashes import via contents <<. Require open-uri (or use a dedicated HTTP client), set timeouts and a max size, and handle nil/failed fetches without raising.

Every cache-miss embed runs a full synchronous feed import

When feed polling is enabled, perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline before the single-URL HTTP fetch. That downloads and imports every feed item on the retrieve job, even though feed_key is computed in PollFeed and never used (no conditional GET). If the feed is slow, invalid, or hits the nil-content crash, the exception aborts perform_retrieve and fetch_http never runs, so turning on feed polling breaks on-demand embeds whenever the feed errors. URL comparison is exact, so a feed link that differs by trailing slash, http/https, or tracking params will not satisfy the embed_url; the expensive poll still runs and fetch_http then creates a second topic for the same article. Fetch the one URL directly, and do not let a feed failure skip that fetch.

Embed lookup is a raw string match and ignores deleted topics

topic_id_for_embed plucks topic_id for an exact embed_url match and does not check that the topic or post still exists. http://host/post, http://host/post/, and the https or utm variants are different rows, so the iframe misses the feed-imported topic and import creates duplicates. After a moderator deletes the topic, the row still matches, EmbedController builds a TopicView for a missing topic instead of enqueueing retrieve, and the URL is stuck. On update (line 32), embed.post is nil once the post is trashed (Post includes Trashable), and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises. That exception is not rescued in PollFeed, so one deleted import stops the hourly feed. Normalize URLs before save/lookup, and treat a missing topic/post as "not embedded" (or destroy the embed row on delete).

Protocol-relative and non-root-relative URLs are rewritten wrong

absolutize_urls treats every href/src that start_with?('/') as a root-relative path and does href.sub(/^\/+/, ''), which strips every leading slash. A protocol-relative image or link such as //cdn.example.com/img.png, which is common in RSS, becomes http://original-host/cdn.example.com/img.png and breaks. Relative URLs that do not start with / (images/a.png, ../a.png) are left untouched, so the browser resolves them against the Discourse origin and they 404 in the topic and in the embed iframe. Only rewrite a single leading slash, leave // URLs as protocol-relative (or prefix the scheme only), and resolve other relative references against the article URL. The same logic is duplicated for img at line 70.

embed_url is varchar(255) but article URLs are often longer

embed_url is a Rails string column, so PostgreSQL stores it as varchar(255), with a unique index on that column. Real article URLs with query parameters routinely exceed 255 characters. TopicEmbed.create! then raises (string truncation / statement invalid), the import transaction rolls back, and the embed stays on the loading page forever because no row is written. Use a text column (and a unique index on text, which PostgreSQL allows) before this ships; a later migration cannot silently widen rows that already failed to insert.

Concurrent imports race and enqueue jobs before commit

import does a check-then-act (where embed_url is blank, then create) inside Topic.transaction. Two retrieve jobs or a poll overlapping a retrieve can both pass the blank check and both call PostCreator. The unique index makes the second TopicEmbed.create! raise, rolling back that savepoint, but PostCreator#create calls enqueue_jobs after its inner transaction returns and before the outer transaction commits. Those Sidekiq jobs are not transactional: they run against a post that is not committed yet or that the unique-violation rollback undoes. The RecordNotUnique exception is also unrescued, so a racing PollFeed aborts the remaining feed items. Rescue the unique violation, re-read the existing embed, and enqueue post-processing only after the outer transaction commits.

Creates do not bypass rate limits that the Disqus importer disables

import passes skip_validations, which only turns off post validations and, in PostCreator, SpamRulesEnforcer. It does not skip RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord on Post. The update path passes bypass_rate_limiter: true, and lib/tasks/disqus.thor calls RateLimiter.disable around the whole import, but PollFeed and TopicRetriever call TopicEmbed.import with the limiter still active. If the embed user is subject to create-topic/create-post limits, a feed larger than that allowance raises mid-loop. PollFeed does not rescue per item and sets retry: false, so the rest of the feed is dropped and the next hourly run fails the same way. Disable the rate limiter for embed/feed creation the same way the Disqus task does, or the hourly import cannot keep up with a normal feed.

Login-required forums redirect the embed iframe to the login page

EmbedController skips check_xhr and preload_json but not the application login_required filter (redirect_to_login_if_required). Comment embeds are loaded anonymously in a third-party iframe. When login_required is on, that request is redirected to the login page before ensure_embeddable runs. The login page is sent with the normal X-Frame-Options policy, so the iframe is blank rather than showing comments. Anonymous readers, which are the main audience for an embedded comment box, never see the discussion. Skip the login redirect for this action and keep the embeddable-host check as the access gate.

Disqus import now requires a live URL and drops category and date

The importer used to create the topic locally from the export (title, permalink body, thread created_at, and optional -c category) and then attach comments, so dead or private links still imported. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which HTTP-fetches t[:link] and parses it with Readability. A 404, timeout, or non-article page skips the entire thread (the comment loop is inside if post.present?). The -c/--category option was removed, and import does not accept category or created_at, so threads land in the default category with "now" as the topic timestamp instead of the Disqus thread date. import_remote also does not require open-uri (see topic_embed.rb). Keep a local fallback when the fetch fails, and pass category and created_at through to PostCreator.

Rails 3 lockfile was not updated for the new embed gems

ruby-readability and simple-rss were added to the Gemfile and to Gemfile_rails4.lock only. RAILS3=1 still uses Gemfile.lock (see the dual-boot lockfile switch at the top of the Gemfile). bundle install --deployment on the Rails 3 path fails because the lockfile does not match the Gemfile, so feed polling and import_remote cannot be installed on that boot path. Update Gemfile.lock as well, or the gems are missing exactly where PollFeed and TopicEmbed require them.

Specs never render embed views or parse a feed

The success examples stub TopicView and do not enable render_views, then an after hook expects HTTP 200. They therefore never compile app/views/embed/best.html.erb, whose `end if` syntax error 500s every real success response. spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only checks that execute sometimes calls poll_feed and never feeds an RSS document, so the nil i.content crash is untested. spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb asserts cooked == raw, which records the unsanitized raw_html behavior instead of asserting that script and event-handler markup is stripped. Add a render_views example and a fixture-based PollFeed/import test that includes a normal RSS item and a hostile HTML body.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue accurately identifies the exact same bug described in the golden comment: passing '80%' as dimensions fails for animated GIFs when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is true because `gifsicle --resize-fit` expects WxH dimensions rather than a percentage, causing downsizing to silently fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile path

OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with tempfile.path as both the source and the destination. The convert command built by downsize_instructions opens the output path for writing before it finishes reading the input, so when those paths are identical ImageMagick truncates the upload and the result is an empty or corrupt image. Versions that special-case this by writing a temporary file and renaming it over the destination leave the already-open Ruby Tempfile descriptor on the old inode while the path points at the new file. Upload.create_for on line 72 is then given that Tempfile object and tempfile.size, so the bytes stored, the SHA1 (if taken from the path), and the recorded filesize can disagree, and the saved upload is not the image the user sent.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying bug: modifying or replacing the file at `tempfile.path` via an external command causes the Ruby `Tempfile` object (`tempfile.size`) to hold stale metadata/size information because its file descriptor still points to the old inode or caches the size. While the candidate focuses slightly more on the corruption/mismatch passed to `Upload.create_for` and the golden comment focuses on the loop termination condition using `tempfile.size`, they both stem from the exact same root cause of `tempfile.size` not reflecting the changes made by `OptimizedImage.downsize` to `tempfile.path`.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize path has no image extension, so encoding and GIF detection fail

create_upload passes tempfile.path straight through and never copies the bytes to a file ending in the original filename's extension. Multipart uploads use Rack's Tempfile (Tempfile.new("RackMultipart")), which has no .jpg/.png/.gif suffix, and the URL branch asks FileHelper.download for a "discourse-upload-#{type}" prefix that also does not include filename's extension. ImageMagick chooses the output encoder from the destination extension, so this convert fails with no encode delegate or writes a payload that is not the format implied by original_filename. optimize only takes the gifsicle path when the source path ends in .gif, so the allow_animation flag passed here does not apply and a GIF is sent through convert's [0] selector, which keeps only the first frame.

Failed downsize is ignored and the file is still uploaded

The loop discards the false return from OptimizedImage.downsize. convert_with returns false when convert, gifsicle, or ImageOptim fails, but the only exit condition is tempfile.size. A convert that truncates the file makes size 0, the while condition ends, and the empty file is treated as small enough and passed to Upload.create_for. If conversion fails without shrinking the file, the loop retries up to five times and then still calls create_for even though the image is larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. downsize_instructions also sets no JPEG -quality, so a re-encode at ImageMagick's default quality can grow the file across attempts. The feature does not enforce the size limit and can persist a truncated or oversized upload.

No maximum size before repeated ImageMagick conversion

The new loop runs for every image larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and never rejects files above the 10MB ceiling added on the client and in the URL downloader. Multipart bodies are not size-capped in create_upload before this work, and the client check is bypassable by a direct POST or API call. Each attempt shells out to convert or gifsicle and then ImageOptim. Any logged-in user can submit a very large image, or a small decompression bomb whose name looks like an image, and force up to five full decodes on a defer thread or, for synchronous API uploads, on a web worker, exhausting CPU and memory before Upload.create_for can apply a filesize error.

URL fetch limit ignores per-type size settings

FileHelper.download used to stop at SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. It now always allows 10.megabytes, and this runs before the code knows whether the URL is an image. Non-image API uploads are not passed through the new downsize loop, so a remote attachment or other non-image is fetched up to 10MB even when max_attachment_size_kb or max_image_size_kb is lower. That raises the amount of data an API client can pull into the temp directory and no longer matches the configured per-type limit.

No tests cover automatic downsize or the new size ceiling

The new behavior — image-only shrinking, a five-attempt 80% loop, what happens when convert fails or the file stays over max_image_size_kb, non-image uploads still bound by their own site setting, and the OptimizedImage.downsize signature change — has no tests in this pull request. A regression that stores a truncated tempfile or rejects a previously allowed attachment would not be caught.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe 500s when the user has no TopicUser row

TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id, topic_id) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. find_by returns nil when that logged-in user has no topic_users row for the topic (never opened it, a different account than the email recipient, or the row was removed). Calling notification_level on nil raises NoMethodError, so the new email link returns 500 instead of unsubscribing or rendering the page. Email delivery usually inserts a row via TopicUser.change, but this public route does not, and nothing here creates one. Use TopicUser.change (it inserts when missing) or handle a missing record, and still persist an explicit muted level.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: `tu` can be `nil` when no `TopicUser` record exists, and calling methods (like `notification_level`) on it will raise a nil/NoMethodError exception.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watching or tracking

The email string says the link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and the page string says "You will stop receiving notifications". The action does not do that. Levels are muted=0, regular=1, tracking=2, watching=3. If the level is above regular it is set to regular; only regular or muted is set to muted. Tracking and regular send the same reply, mention, and quote emails, so a tracking user who clicks the link is unchanged and keeps those emails. A watching user is only dropped to regular and still gets reply, mention, and quote mail for the topic. The GET is also not idempotent: a refresh or second fetch sees regular and then mutes, so the result depends on how many times the URL is hit, and neither the email nor the page describes a two-step downgrade. The client route never changes the level itself, so an in-app transition to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe only shows that future-tense copy. To match the copy, one request should set the topic to muted.

Direct save lets auto-track undo the unsubscribe

The action assigns notification_level and calls save!. TopicUser.change is what records a user-chosen level: it sets notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed when it is still nil, and publishes on MessageBus. save! does none of that. update_last_read's SQL and TopicUser.auto_track only auto-upgrade a topic to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null. A row created just to store last_emailed_post_number still has a null reason. After this sets muted or regular, the next read that crosses an enabled auto-track threshold (user auto_track_topics_after_msecs or the site setting >= 0) writes tracking back, so the unsubscribe does not stick and notifications resume. Other open tabs also keep the old level because MessageBus is not notified. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so it is stored as an explicit user choice.

Topic unsubscribe mutates notification level on GET

config/routes.rb exposes GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, and the action writes notification_level before rendering. There is no per-user token and no CSRF token. The URL is predictable from the topic slug and id, and protect_from_forgery does not apply to GET. In this app's era, browsers send session cookies on cross-site GETs, so another site can change a logged-in user's topic level with an img, redirect, or top-level link. A prefetch that includes the session does the same without a click. Because the downgrade is not idempotent, two fetches can go from watching to regular and then to muted. Do not change state on GET; show a confirmation and mutate on POST, or require an unguessable one-time key plus an explicit confirm.

Shared render drops canonical URL on every topic page

show calls perform_show_response and only then calls canonical_url(...) with the topic canonical path, discarding the return value. That call exists to store the URL the layout emits (Discourse assigns @canonical_url for rel=canonical / og:url) before render. Rendering used to be implicit at the end of the action, after that call. This change adds render :show inside perform_show_response's HTML branch, which show and unsubscribe both use, so the topic template and layout run before canonical_url. Every normal topic HTML response is sent without its canonical link. That is an SEO regression for all topic pages, not just unsubscribe. Set the canonical URL before rendering, or render only from unsubscribe after show's post-setup has run.

Unsubscribe template path does not match the Ember route

app-route-map.js.es6 registers a top-level route named topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe. Ember resolves that route's template from the dasherized name topic-unsubscribe (underscore/dasherize of topicUnsubscribe, not a slash path). The new route, controller, and view files use that name (topic-unsubscribe.js.es6), but the template is templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is registered as topic/unsubscribe — the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route that was never defined. After the server handles the email link, the Ember app will not find a template and will error instead of showing the confirmation text and the topic-notifications-button. Put the template at templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route as topic.unsubscribe and move the controller and view to match.

No spec checks unsubscribe behavior or the new email link

The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder so the updated unsubscribe_link translation does not raise MissingInterpolationArgument, then still only asserts that the user-preferences URL is in the body. It never checks that the topic unsubscribe URL or the new "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" sentence is present. There is no controller or request spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus tracking versus regular, a second request stepping down again, the slug redirect, or notifications_reason_id being set. Those paths are currently untested and are where this feature fails.

The value written back is accessTokenParsed.data; with sharing enabled that object has been reduced to access_token plus a fabricated refresh_token, so instance_url and the other Salesforce fields are dropped from the saved key.
