true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Header panel is not pinned right in the 2009 flexbox the new mixin enables

.d-header .panel no longer has float: right, and .d-header .title no longer has float: left. The replacement is margin-left: auto on .panel inside a .contents flex container, plus order. Auto margins absorb free space in modern flexbox and in IE10 (-ms-flexbox), so current Chrome, Firefox, Safari 7+, and IE10 still pin the icons to the right. They do not in the 2009 model: display: -webkit-box and display: -moz-box, which the new flexbox() mixin emits, treat auto margins as 0 and only distribute space with box-flex / -webkit-box-flex, which is never set. Browsers that only understand those prefixes (Safari 6, iOS 6, Android 4.3 stock browser, Firefox 21 and older) pack the logo, topic info, and controls on the left instead of keeping the menu at the right edge. Browsers with no flexbox at all lose the float fallback and stack the logo and panel as normal blocks. Keep float: left / float: right as the non-flex fallback (a flex formatting context ignores float on the items) and drop the 2009 display values, or add a 2009 pack so those prefixes actually reproduce the header.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment's core point is that removing float: right on .d-header .panel breaks alignment in non-flex contexts, such as the noscript header where .panel is not a flex item. The candidate also flags the removed float fallback for .panel and .title. It notes that browsers without flexbox lose that fallback and stack the logo and panel, and it recommends keeping the floats. That is the same underlying concern, though the candidate frames it around older browsers rather than the noscript markup.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items() mixin emits an invalid property and skips old Firefox

align-items() copies one keyword into every prefix and emits -ms-align-items, which is not a CSS property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, already set above). Old Firefox, which flexbox() and inline-flex() target with display: -moz-box and display: -moz-inline-box, needs -moz-box-align, and that declaration is missing. Header .contents, .small-action, and .badge-wrapper.bullet therefore become 2009 boxes with no cross-axis alignment in that engine, so the vertical centering and bullet baseline alignment this PR adds do not apply. The 2009 and IE10 properties also do not accept modern keywords: flex-start and flex-end must be mapped to start and end for -webkit-box-align, -moz-box-align, and -ms-flex-align, while -webkit-align-items and align-items keep the modern names. center and baseline happen to be valid in all three syntaxes, so IE10 and old WebKit align for the current call sites, but the mixin is wrong for the other standard values.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says that -ms-align-items is not a CSS property and that IE10 uses -ms-flex-align instead. This is the same issue the golden comment raises.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin is off by one for 2009 box-ordinal-group

order() writes $val straight through to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (initial value 1, legal values are integers >= 1); standard order is 0-based (initial value 0). The matching prefix is $val + 1. As written, order(0) emits box-ordinal-group: 0, which is invalid and dropped so the item stays in the default group; order(1) ties with unordered siblings instead of following them; a negative order, the usual way to pull an item to the front, is invalid and ignored. -ms-flex-order and -webkit-order correctly share order's numbering, so IE10 and 2012-spec WebKit are fine. Header callers pass 2 and 3, which still sort after default items in both systems, but the mixin does not implement order for any other value. Add 1 on the two box-ordinal-group declarations.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: box-ordinal-group is 1-based, so passing $val straight through breaks the value 0 and causes incorrect ordering in older browsers.

false_positives.candidate:
Flexbox on .small-action unpins the action button and shrink-wraps the description

.small-action is now a flex container (display:flex via the new flexbox mixin, align-items:center), and .small-action-desc is no longer a full-width block. Its padding changed from 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em to 0 1.5%, and it has no flex-grow, so it shrink-wraps to its text. The staff delete/recover control is positioned only by .small-action button { float: right }, which used to pin it to the right edge of that full-width row. Float does not apply to flex items, so a button that is a direct child stays in source order beside the label; a button nested in .small-action-desc only floats to the right of the shrink-wrapped description, not the post row. On short actions the control sits against or over the label instead of at the far right. Set flex: 1 and min-width: 0 on .small-action-desc so an inner float can still reach the row edge, or drop the float and push the button with margin-left: auto.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is never called

ActiveModel::Serializers includes an attribute only if include_<name>? returns true. Every other hook in this serializer uses that form (include_email?, include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, and the methods defined by untrusted_attributes). include_website_name has no question mark, so it is never invoked and the website.present? guard is dead code. website_name is therefore always serialized, including a null website_name when the user has no website or the host cannot be parsed. The omission the new method was written to provide cannot happen.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate pinpoints the missing ? suffix on include_website_name, which means the conditional inclusion never takes effect. That is the main issue in the golden comment. The golden comment's second point, about string mutation, is extra and does not change the match on the primary issue.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous website hiding

website_name is computed from the profile website and added as a public attribute, but it is not registered in untrusted_attributes, which is what suppresses website for anonymous viewers of trust-level 0 users. include_website_name also never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?. Previously the profile label was derived in the browser from model.website, so omitting website also omitted the label. After this change, an anonymous GET of a TL0 user still receives website_name (the hostname, and host plus path when the same-domain branch matches) even though website is withheld. That discloses the URL the serializer is supposed to hide; with the path appended, the withheld URL can be reconstructed. The profile template will render that text. The spec's TL0 example still only asserts that website is absent and never checks website_name, so the regression is untested. Adding the missing ? on the include hook is not enough: that method only checks website.present?, which is true in this case.

Same-domain check mismatches common hosts

The decision to append the URL path does not compare registrable domains, so it both over-matches and under-matches. The elsif treats hosts as the same site when they have the same label count greater than 2 and share every label after the first. That equates unrelated sites that only share a public suffix: a forum at forum.co.uk and a website of http://phishing.co.uk/login both reduce to co.uk, so the profile shows phishing.co.uk/login instead of phishing.co.uk. The same false positive applies to *.com.au, *.co.jp, *.blogspot.com, *.github.io, and similar. The else branch only checks discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host), so the path is added when the website is a parent of the forum, but not when the website is a subdomain of the forum. A forum at example.com with website http://www.example.com/docs or http://blog.example.com/users/jane displays only www.example.com or blog.example.com, which hides the path this change is meant to show. Comparison is also case-sensitive: URI#host is lowercased, but Discourse.current_hostname is not normalized here, so a mixed-case hostname fails the exact-match branch and drops the path. The new specs only cover an unrelated host, an exact match, and the website-is-parent direction; they never exercise the elsif or the www/subdomain cases.

Non-ASCII website URLs vanish from the profile

The host is parsed with URI(...).host rescue nil, and a nil host makes website_name return nil. The profile template now shows the globe and link only when model.website_name is present, with no fallback to model.website. Ruby's stdlib URI raises URI::InvalidURIError on non-ASCII input (for example http://例え.jp/path) and on URLs containing spaces; those errors are swallowed, so website_name is null and the link disappears even though website is still stored and is still serialized for viewers allowed to see it. The old client label used website.split("/")[2], which still displayed a hostname for those strings. Internationalized profile websites that previously appeared are now omitted until rewritten as ASCII or punycode.

Website label goes stale after website changes

The header used to label the site with a controller computed property that observed model.website and updated when the website changed. It now renders the server field model.website_name, which is copied onto the model only when the user payload is first loaded. User#save sends the new website but only copies bio_excerpt back from the PUT response, so it never refreshes website_name. The header lives in user.hbs outside {{outlet}} and stays visible on preferences and other child routes. After model.website changes, the anchor href is the new URL while the link text is still the previous website_name until a full reload, so the visible label can name a different host than the link destination.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check is an inverted substring test

postMessageReceived accepts the event when discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is not -1, i.e. when the configured URL string contains the sender origin. That is the opposite of an origin allowlist and also ignores e.source, so it is not limited to this iframe. Any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl is treated as trusted. If discourseUrl is http://forum.example.com:3000/, a page at http://forum.example.com (port 80) matches at index 0 and can set iframe.height. Compare parsed origins for equality and require e.source === iframe.contentWindow. The same file concatenates discourseUrl + "embed/best" with no slash normalization (line 7), so a discourseUrl without a trailing slash requests a non-existent host path and the embed 404s.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the indexOf-based postMessage origin check as weak and bypassable. The golden comment's specific example (evil-discourseUrl.com) assumes the reverse direction. The candidate correctly reads it as discourseUrl.indexOf(origin), which makes prefix origins trusted. The underlying issue is the same: insufficient indexOf origin validation that can be bypassed.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized (stored XSS)

TopicEmbed.import appends an attribution link by interpolating the raw URL into HTML (href='#{url}' and the link text), then PostCreator stores that string with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations. Post#cook (post.rb:133) returns raw unchanged for raw_html, skipping the markdown sanitizer and plugin filters. The embed view prints it with raw post.cooked (best.html.erb:19), and the normal topic page also treats cooked as HTML, so the payload runs on the Discourse origin for every viewer. The URL is attacker-controlled: /embed/best only checks a spoofable Referer host, then the retrieve job accepts any http(s) URL whose host equals embeddable_host. A URL Ruby will parse, such as http://eviltrout.com/?q='onmouseover='alert(1), still returns the real page on most blogs (query string ignored) and, after Nokogiri::HTML.fragment.to_html, becomes an anchor with an event-handler attribute. absolutize_urls does not strip script, on* attributes, or javascript: URLs. The RSS path is worse: PollFeed does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) and imports that with no allowlist at all, so a feed body of <script> becomes a live script tag. import_remote's readability tag list still keeps a[href] and img[src], so javascript: links survive. Escaping the footer URL is required but not sufficient; sanitize imported HTML before it is persisted as cooked, including on the update path.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment raises two issues: a nil contents NoMethodError and XSS from unescaped URL interpolation. The candidate explicitly identifies the XSS from the raw URL interpolated into the href and link text in TopicEmbed.import. It does not mention the nil case, but it matches the XSS part of the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Success template has invalid Ruby (`end if`) and cannot render

The header branch is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby. ERB compiles the template before running it, so every successful embed (topic already imported, TopicView assigned) raises a syntax/template error instead of showing comments. The loading template is valid, so the iframe sits on "Loading Discussion..." until retrieve finishes and then 500s. The matching closer must be `<% end %>`. spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb never enables render_views, so it still expects 200 and will not catch this.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: the ERB block is closed with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby and makes rendering fail. Both say the fix is a plain `end`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
RSS poll crashes because item content is often nil

poll_feed always does i.content.scrub and then CGI.unescapeHTML. SimpleRSS leaves content nil for ordinary RSS 2.0 items (body is description and/or content_encoded) and for Atom entries that only have a summary. nil.scrub raises NoMethodError. There is no per-item rescue, and the job sets sidekiq retry: false, so one such item aborts the rest of the feed and the same crash repeats every hour. String#scrub also does not exist before Ruby 2.1, so this line fails even when content is present on 1.9/2.0. Use description / content / content_encoded with a nil guard, rescue per item, and do not let one bad entry (nil body, nil/short title, URI error, rate limit) skip the remainder. open(feed_url) also has no timeout, so a hung feed blocks the scheduler indefinitely.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate flags the same bug: i.content can be nil, so i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError. It also proposes the same fix, falling back to description. The extra points it raises do not change this match.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Referer is interpolated into a script string (reflected XSS)

The embed layout writes request.referer into a single-quoted JavaScript string with <%= %>. On Rails 3.2 and 4.0 that helper escapes &, <, >, and double quotes, but not single quotes, and it is not a JavaScript escape. ensure_embeddable only checks that URI(referer).host equals SiteSetting.embeddable_host, and Ruby's URI parser allows ' and () in the query. A parent URL such as http://eviltrout.com/?x=';alert(document.domain);// therefore passes the host check and is rendered as parent.postMessage(..., 'http://eviltrout.com/?x=';alert(document.domain);//'); which runs in the Discourse origin. This layout wraps both the loading and best responses, and a normal blog page that includes the embed script sends the full parent URL (including query string) as Referer. Any logged-in user who opens a crafted link on the embeddable host executes attacker script in the iframe and can perform forum actions as that user. Pass a fixed origin (Discourse base URL) or JSON-encode the target origin; do not HTML-interpolate a request header into script.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same flaw: request.referer is interpolated unescaped into JavaScript in the embed layout, which allows XSS.

false_positives.candidate:
Spoofable Referer is enough to fetch URLs and create topics

best enqueues retrieve_topic for any embed_url when the Referer host matches embeddable_host. Referer is fully client-controlled, the route is an unauthenticated GET, and TopicRetriever only compares URI(embed_url).host to that setting (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15). It does not restrict scheme beyond what open accepts, port, path, or redirects. import_remote then calls open(url).read (topic_embed.rb:48). open-uri follows redirects to other hosts by default, so an open redirect on the embeddable host (or a 302 to link-local/metadata addresses) becomes server-side request forgery, including port probes such as http://embeddable-host:6379/. The 60s throttle key is per URL, so an attacker can enqueue a distinct job and create a distinct public topic for every query string that returns HTTP 200, all as embed_by_username, bypassing SpamRulesEnforcer because import passes skip_validations. There is no body size limit or timeout, so this is also a memory/job-queue DoS. Require a non-spoofable control (signed embed token), re-validate every redirect hop against an allowlist, cap response size, and rate-limit imports globally.

import_remote uses Kernel#open without requiring open-uri

import_remote fetches the article with open(url).read but never requires open-uri. Kernel#open only treats the argument as an HTTP URL after open-uri is loaded; otherwise it opens a local path and raises Errno::ENOENT, so no topic is created. poll_feed.rb requires open-uri at load time, and TopicRetriever calls PollFeed before fetch_http only when feed polling is enabled, so on-demand import accidentally depends on that file having been loaded in-process. The Disqus thor task calls import_remote without requiring open-uri either. The call also has no read timeout or byte limit, and a nil doc.content then crashes import via contents <<. Require open-uri (or use a dedicated HTTP client), set timeouts and a max size, and handle nil/failed fetches without raising.

Every cache-miss embed runs a full synchronous feed import

When feed polling is enabled, perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline before the single-URL HTTP fetch. That downloads and imports every feed item on the retrieve job, even though feed_key is computed in PollFeed and never used (no conditional GET). If the feed is slow, invalid, or hits the nil-content crash, the exception aborts perform_retrieve and fetch_http never runs, so turning on feed polling breaks on-demand embeds whenever the feed errors. URL comparison is exact, so a feed link that differs by trailing slash, http/https, or tracking params will not satisfy the embed_url; the expensive poll still runs and fetch_http then creates a second topic for the same article. Fetch the one URL directly, and do not let a feed failure skip that fetch.

Embed lookup is a raw string match and ignores deleted topics

topic_id_for_embed plucks topic_id for an exact embed_url match and does not check that the topic or post still exists. http://host/post, http://host/post/, and the https or utm variants are different rows, so the iframe misses the feed-imported topic and import creates duplicates. After a moderator deletes the topic, the row still matches, EmbedController builds a TopicView for a missing topic instead of enqueueing retrieve, and the URL is stuck. On update (line 32), embed.post is nil once the post is trashed (Post includes Trashable), and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises. That exception is not rescued in PollFeed, so one deleted import stops the hourly feed. Normalize URLs before save/lookup, and treat a missing topic/post as "not embedded" (or destroy the embed row on delete).

Protocol-relative and non-root-relative URLs are rewritten wrong

absolutize_urls treats every href/src that start_with?('/') as a root-relative path and does href.sub(/^\/+/, ''), which strips every leading slash. A protocol-relative image or link such as //cdn.example.com/img.png, which is common in RSS, becomes http://original-host/cdn.example.com/img.png and breaks. Relative URLs that do not start with / (images/a.png, ../a.png) are left untouched, so the browser resolves them against the Discourse origin and they 404 in the topic and in the embed iframe. Only rewrite a single leading slash, leave // URLs as protocol-relative (or prefix the scheme only), and resolve other relative references against the article URL. The same logic is duplicated for img at line 70.

embed_url is varchar(255) but article URLs are often longer

embed_url is a Rails string column, so PostgreSQL stores it as varchar(255), with a unique index on that column. Real article URLs with query parameters routinely exceed 255 characters. TopicEmbed.create! then raises (string truncation / statement invalid), the import transaction rolls back, and the embed stays on the loading page forever because no row is written. Use a text column (and a unique index on text, which PostgreSQL allows) before this ships; a later migration cannot silently widen rows that already failed to insert.

Concurrent imports race and enqueue jobs before commit

import does a check-then-act (where embed_url is blank, then create) inside Topic.transaction. Two retrieve jobs or a poll overlapping a retrieve can both pass the blank check and both call PostCreator. The unique index makes the second TopicEmbed.create! raise, rolling back that savepoint, but PostCreator#create calls enqueue_jobs after its inner transaction returns and before the outer transaction commits. Those Sidekiq jobs are not transactional: they run against a post that is not committed yet or that the unique-violation rollback undoes. The RecordNotUnique exception is also unrescued, so a racing PollFeed aborts the remaining feed items. Rescue the unique violation, re-read the existing embed, and enqueue post-processing only after the outer transaction commits.

Creates do not bypass rate limits that the Disqus importer disables

import passes skip_validations, which only turns off post validations and, in PostCreator, SpamRulesEnforcer. It does not skip RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord on Post. The update path passes bypass_rate_limiter: true, and lib/tasks/disqus.thor calls RateLimiter.disable around the whole import, but PollFeed and TopicRetriever call TopicEmbed.import with the limiter still active. If the embed user is subject to create-topic/create-post limits, a feed larger than that allowance raises mid-loop. PollFeed does not rescue per item and sets retry: false, so the rest of the feed is dropped and the next hourly run fails the same way. Disable the rate limiter for embed/feed creation the same way the Disqus task does, or the hourly import cannot keep up with a normal feed.

Login-required forums redirect the embed iframe to the login page

EmbedController skips check_xhr and preload_json but not the application login_required filter (redirect_to_login_if_required). Comment embeds are loaded anonymously in a third-party iframe. When login_required is on, that request is redirected to the login page before ensure_embeddable runs. The login page is sent with the normal X-Frame-Options policy, so the iframe is blank rather than showing comments. Anonymous readers, which are the main audience for an embedded comment box, never see the discussion. Skip the login redirect for this action and keep the embeddable-host check as the access gate.

Disqus import now requires a live URL and drops category and date

The importer used to create the topic locally from the export (title, permalink body, thread created_at, and optional -c category) and then attach comments, so dead or private links still imported. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which HTTP-fetches t[:link] and parses it with Readability. A 404, timeout, or non-article page skips the entire thread (the comment loop is inside if post.present?). The -c/--category option was removed, and import does not accept category or created_at, so threads land in the default category with "now" as the topic timestamp instead of the Disqus thread date. import_remote also does not require open-uri (see topic_embed.rb). Keep a local fallback when the fetch fails, and pass category and created_at through to PostCreator.

Rails 3 lockfile was not updated for the new embed gems

ruby-readability and simple-rss were added to the Gemfile and to Gemfile_rails4.lock only. RAILS3=1 still uses Gemfile.lock (see the dual-boot lockfile switch at the top of the Gemfile). bundle install --deployment on the Rails 3 path fails because the lockfile does not match the Gemfile, so feed polling and import_remote cannot be installed on that boot path. Update Gemfile.lock as well, or the gems are missing exactly where PollFeed and TopicEmbed require them.

Specs never render embed views or parse a feed

The success examples stub TopicView and do not enable render_views, then an after hook expects HTTP 200. They therefore never compile app/views/embed/best.html.erb, whose `end if` syntax error 500s every real success response. spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only checks that execute sometimes calls poll_feed and never feeds an RSS document, so the nil i.content crash is untested. spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb asserts cooked == raw, which records the unsanitized raw_html behavior instead of asserting that script and event-handler markup is stripped. Add a render_views example and a fixture-based PollFeed/import test that includes a normal RSS item and a hostile HTML body.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API

Ruby does not overload by arity, so def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) on line 149 replaces def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) on line 145 at load time and emits a method-redefined warning. The width/height implementation is dead. This class previously exposed downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts). Callers that still pass width, height, and an options hash now raise ArgumentError (5 arguments for a method that accepts at most 4). Callers that pass width and height only bind height to opts, and optimize then raises TypeError on opts[:allow_animation] because an Integer does not accept a Symbol index. The new uploads-controller call only works because it matches the surviving definition; definition order, not an overload, is what makes "80%" work.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem: the second downsize definition, which takes a dimensions parameter, overrides the first, which takes width and height. This leaves the original unreachable and breaks callers that pass width and height separately.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type

validateUploadedFile used to compare against Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments honored separate admin limits. It now always uses 10 * 1024 KB. Attachments larger than max_attachment_size_kb but under 10MB pass the client and are not downsized by the new server loop; attachments that the admin allowed above 10MB are rejected. Images are capped at 10MB even if max_image_size_kb is higher, and a max_image_size_kb of 0 (which skips server downsize because the new guard requires > 0) still hits this fixed client cap. The 413 handler on line 246 repeats the same constant, so the user-facing file_too_large message always claims the maximum is 10240 KB even when the proxy or the site setting rejected the file for a different limit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem: the hardcoded 10*1024 KB limit replaces the per-type site setting, so the client-side check diverges from the configured limits. Both also note that the 413 handler repeats the same constant.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
80% geometry and thumbnail setting do not correctly downsize GIFs

The third argument is the ImageMagick percentage "80%", but when the path ends in .gif and allow_animation is true, optimize uses gifsicle --resize-fit with that string. --resize-fit is built for a pixel box such as 800x600 (resize_instructions_animated), not an ImageMagick percentage, so the animated shrink fails and, because the return value is ignored, the GIF is left over the size limit. allow_animation is also bound to SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. When that thumbnail setting is off, the canonical upload goes through convert's [0] frame selector and the stored GIF silently loses every frame but the first, even though the setting is not supposed to rewrite originals.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate raises the same problem as the golden comment. It says that '80%' is passed to gifsicle's --resize-fit when the animated path is used, that --resize-fit expects WxH geometry, and that the downsize therefore fails silently. The extra point about the thumbnail setting does not change this match.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile path

OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with tempfile.path as both the source and the destination. The convert command built by downsize_instructions opens the output path for writing before it finishes reading the input, so when those paths are identical ImageMagick truncates the upload and the result is an empty or corrupt image. Versions that special-case this by writing a temporary file and renaming it over the destination leave the already-open Ruby Tempfile descriptor on the old inode while the path points at the new file. Upload.create_for on line 72 is then given that Tempfile object and tempfile.size, so the bytes stored, the SHA1 (if taken from the path), and the recorded filesize can disagree, and the saved upload is not the image the user sent.

Downsize path has no image extension, so encoding and GIF detection fail

create_upload passes tempfile.path straight through and never copies the bytes to a file ending in the original filename's extension. Multipart uploads use Rack's Tempfile (Tempfile.new("RackMultipart")), which has no .jpg/.png/.gif suffix, and the URL branch asks FileHelper.download for a "discourse-upload-#{type}" prefix that also does not include filename's extension. ImageMagick chooses the output encoder from the destination extension, so this convert fails with no encode delegate or writes a payload that is not the format implied by original_filename. optimize only takes the gifsicle path when the source path ends in .gif, so the allow_animation flag passed here does not apply and a GIF is sent through convert's [0] selector, which keeps only the first frame.

Failed downsize is ignored and the file is still uploaded

The loop discards the false return from OptimizedImage.downsize. convert_with returns false when convert, gifsicle, or ImageOptim fails, but the only exit condition is tempfile.size. A convert that truncates the file makes size 0, the while condition ends, and the empty file is treated as small enough and passed to Upload.create_for. If conversion fails without shrinking the file, the loop retries up to five times and then still calls create_for even though the image is larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. downsize_instructions also sets no JPEG -quality, so a re-encode at ImageMagick's default quality can grow the file across attempts. The feature does not enforce the size limit and can persist a truncated or oversized upload.

No maximum size before repeated ImageMagick conversion

The new loop runs for every image larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and never rejects files above the 10MB ceiling added on the client and in the URL downloader. Multipart bodies are not size-capped in create_upload before this work, and the client check is bypassable by a direct POST or API call. Each attempt shells out to convert or gifsicle and then ImageOptim. Any logged-in user can submit a very large image, or a small decompression bomb whose name looks like an image, and force up to five full decodes on a defer thread or, for synchronous API uploads, on a web worker, exhausting CPU and memory before Upload.create_for can apply a filesize error.

URL fetch limit ignores per-type size settings

FileHelper.download used to stop at SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. It now always allows 10.megabytes, and this runs before the code knows whether the URL is an image. Non-image API uploads are not passed through the new downsize loop, so a remote attachment or other non-image is fetched up to 10MB even when max_attachment_size_kb or max_image_size_kb is lower. That raises the amount of data an API client can pull into the temp directory and no longer matches the configured per-type limit.

No tests cover automatic downsize or the new size ceiling

The new behavior — image-only shrinking, a five-attempt 80% loop, what happens when convert fails or the file stays over max_image_size_kb, non-image uploads still bound by their own site setting, and the OptimizedImage.downsize signature change — has no tests in this pull request. A regression that stores a truncated tempfile or rejects a previously allowed attachment would not be caught.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe 500s when the user has no TopicUser row

TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id, topic_id) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. find_by returns nil when that logged-in user has no topic_users row for the topic (never opened it, a different account than the email recipient, or the row was removed). Calling notification_level on nil raises NoMethodError, so the new email link returns 500 instead of unsubscribing or rendering the page. Email delivery usually inserts a row via TopicUser.change, but this public route does not, and nothing here creates one. Use TopicUser.change (it inserts when missing) or handle a missing record, and still persist an explicit muted level.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when no record exists, and calling a method on that nil crashes. The candidate words it as a NoMethodError and a 500 response, but the underlying issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watching or tracking

The email string says the link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and the page string says "You will stop receiving notifications". The action does not do that. Levels are muted=0, regular=1, tracking=2, watching=3. If the level is above regular it is set to regular; only regular or muted is set to muted. Tracking and regular send the same reply, mention, and quote emails, so a tracking user who clicks the link is unchanged and keeps those emails. A watching user is only dropped to regular and still gets reply, mention, and quote mail for the topic. The GET is also not idempotent: a refresh or second fetch sees regular and then mutes, so the result depends on how many times the URL is hit, and neither the email nor the page describes a two-step downgrade. The client route never changes the level itself, so an in-app transition to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe only shows that future-tense copy. To match the copy, one request should set the topic to muted.

Direct save lets auto-track undo the unsubscribe

The action assigns notification_level and calls save!. TopicUser.change is what records a user-chosen level: it sets notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed when it is still nil, and publishes on MessageBus. save! does none of that. update_last_read's SQL and TopicUser.auto_track only auto-upgrade a topic to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null. A row created just to store last_emailed_post_number still has a null reason. After this sets muted or regular, the next read that crosses an enabled auto-track threshold (user auto_track_topics_after_msecs or the site setting >= 0) writes tracking back, so the unsubscribe does not stick and notifications resume. Other open tabs also keep the old level because MessageBus is not notified. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so it is stored as an explicit user choice.

Topic unsubscribe mutates notification level on GET

config/routes.rb exposes GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, and the action writes notification_level before rendering. There is no per-user token and no CSRF token. The URL is predictable from the topic slug and id, and protect_from_forgery does not apply to GET. In this app's era, browsers send session cookies on cross-site GETs, so another site can change a logged-in user's topic level with an img, redirect, or top-level link. A prefetch that includes the session does the same without a click. Because the downgrade is not idempotent, two fetches can go from watching to regular and then to muted. Do not change state on GET; show a confirmation and mutate on POST, or require an unguessable one-time key plus an explicit confirm.

Shared render drops canonical URL on every topic page

show calls perform_show_response and only then calls canonical_url(...) with the topic canonical path, discarding the return value. That call exists to store the URL the layout emits (Discourse assigns @canonical_url for rel=canonical / og:url) before render. Rendering used to be implicit at the end of the action, after that call. This change adds render :show inside perform_show_response's HTML branch, which show and unsubscribe both use, so the topic template and layout run before canonical_url. Every normal topic HTML response is sent without its canonical link. That is an SEO regression for all topic pages, not just unsubscribe. Set the canonical URL before rendering, or render only from unsubscribe after show's post-setup has run.

Unsubscribe template path does not match the Ember route

app-route-map.js.es6 registers a top-level route named topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe. Ember resolves that route's template from the dasherized name topic-unsubscribe (underscore/dasherize of topicUnsubscribe, not a slash path). The new route, controller, and view files use that name (topic-unsubscribe.js.es6), but the template is templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is registered as topic/unsubscribe — the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route that was never defined. After the server handles the email link, the Ember app will not find a template and will error instead of showing the confirmation text and the topic-notifications-button. Put the template at templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route as topic.unsubscribe and move the controller and view to match.

No spec checks unsubscribe behavior or the new email link

The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder so the updated unsubscribe_link translation does not raise MissingInterpolationArgument, then still only asserts that the user-preferences URL is in the body. It never checks that the topic unsubscribe URL or the new "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" sentence is present. There is no controller or request spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus tracking versus regular, a second request stepping down again, the slug redirect, or notifications_reason_id being set. Those paths are currently untested and are where this feature fails.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Empty updateMany throws after cache is written

fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache ends by calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Prisma Client rejects updateMany when data is an empty object (validation error: data needs at least one field), and updateMany does not apply @updatedAt anyway, so {} cannot bump the column. unwatchCalendar in this file calls fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache after deleting cache, and Google webhook/cron refresh uses the same method. Those flows now throw after CalendarCache rows have already been upserted, so a successful cache write is reported as a failure and retried. The new UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so this call does not serve the feature; remove it, or if the touch is required pass { updatedAt: new Date() } using UpdateManyMutationInput (the new repository method is typed as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which allows relation ops updateMany cannot apply).
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the updateManyByCredentialId call with an empty data object. Both say it fails to bump updatedAt and suggest explicitly setting updatedAt: new Date(). The candidate adds extra claims (that it throws, and that it has UI relevance), but the core issue is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook helper writes the wrong .env and fails on Linux

ENV_FILE is the relative path "../.env", resolved from the process cwd rather than the script directory. Running ./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root (the usual invocation) creates or edits a .env outside the repository and never sets GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL where the app reads it; it can also modify an unrelated project's env file. The update on line 68 uses sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed on Linux errors and does not update the file. cleanup() then exits 0 even when URL extraction fails, so the failure is easy to miss.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate says sed -i '' is BSD/macOS syntax and fails with GNU sed on Linux. That is the same issue as the golden comment. The candidate also raises other issues, but this one is included.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete cache leaves stale status in the UI

deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper loads that query with refetchOnWindowFocus: false and passes onChanged through as an optional prop, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old cacheUpdatedAt and the delete action. Users are told the cache was deleted while the page keeps offering to delete it until a full remount.

Cache status treats expired rows as live cache

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache by credentialId and returns max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter. Availability reads (getCachedAvailability) ignore rows whose expiresAt is in the past, but those rows are not deleted. Any leftover expired row still yields a cacheUpdatedAt, and CredentialActionsDropdown treats a truthy cacheUpdatedAt as live cache. Google connections whose cache has expired still show "Last updated" and "Delete cached data" even though that cache is not served.

updatedAt backfill marks every existing cache as just written

The migration adds CalendarCache.updatedAt NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(). Every existing row, including stale or expired cache, receives the migration transaction time rather than when the cache value was actually written. The new UI displays that column as "Last updated", so after deploy every Google credential that has any CalendarCache row looks freshly synced until the next Prisma upsert. The leading comment is also wrong: it says the column is added without a default and cannot be applied to a non-empty table, but the SQL does add a default. Backfill from a real write time, or leave the column nullable so legacy rows show as unknown instead of a false timestamp.

In-memory delegation calendars cannot see or delete cache

Cache status is loaded only via connectedCalendars.map(cal => cal.credentialId) and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. In-memory delegation credentials use negative credential IDs: calendar-cache.repository.ts treats credentialId < 0 as invalid for DB writes and reads those users' cache by userId plus key, not by the synthetic id. The status query therefore returns nothing for those connections, so the dropdown never shows cache. deleteCache.handler.ts (credential lookup where id = credentialId and userId = session user) also cannot find an in-memory delegation credential and throws "Credential not found or access denied". Org users on delegated Google Calendar cannot view or clear the cache this feature is meant to manage.

No tests for deleteCache ownership check

deleteCache is a new mutation that deletes every CalendarCache row for a credential after a single findFirst on id plus userId, and the PR adds no tests. Nothing asserts that another user's credentialId is rejected, that a missing credential deletes zero rows, or that a negative in-memory delegation id is denied. That where clause is the only authorization control; a regression would wipe another user's calendar cache without the suite catching it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours check rejects split schedules and ignores duration

The new working-hours gate uses workingHours.find and treats a match as "outside hours" (lines 139-150). The callback returns true when the slot's UTC weekday is in an entry and the slot start is outside that one range. find therefore succeeds if any same-day window does not contain the slot. A normal lunch-break schedule (two rows such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same weekdays) rejects every slot, because each slot misses at least one window. This runs for all fixed hosts, including 1:1 events, so those users see no bookable times. The end minute is also copied from the slot start (line 142 uses slotStartTime for both start and end) instead of the slot end, so event length is never compared to the window end and a round-robin slot taken from a longer host can run past the fixed host's hours. A weekday with no matching entry is not rejected at all, so a fixed host with no hours that day is treated as free when the slot came from someone else.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says the end minute is copied from slotStartTime instead of the slot end. That is the same bug the golden comment describes.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Override containment is inverted for multiple ranges

Date overrides are scanned with find (lines 106-130), and a truthy callback is treated as "slot is not within the override", which makes checkIfIsAvailable return false. The callback returns true when the slot is outside a single range (ends at or before that range's start, or starts after that range's end). Two override windows on the same day, which is how a break is stored, therefore disqualify every slot: each slot is outside at least one range, so the fixed host has no availability that day. A slot is also treated as inside a range unless it is completely before or completely after it, so a slot that only partially overlaps (starts before the window and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it) is accepted and can extend past the override. The all-day block on line 114 compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and never succeeds, so a zero-length override is not reliably treated as an all-day block.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate's main point is a different logic issue, but it also says the all-day check compares dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and never succeeds. That is the same bug the golden comment describes.

false_positives.candidate:
Date-override hit returns available and skips busy times

checkIfIsAvailable returns true as soon as any date override is considered to cover the slot (the dateOverrideExist branch around line 133), before the busy-interval loop. Busy times from calendars and existing bookings are the only conflict filter applied to slots generated from working hours, and this function is that filter. It runs for every fixed host, which includes ordinary 1:1 and collective events (non-round-robin users are marked isFixed), and again for round-robin non-fixed hosts. On any day a host has a date override, slots during meetings are shown as free and can be double-booked.

Override timezone shift keeps only clock time and can wipe the day

The new conversion adds inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset to the override instants and then stores only .hour() and .minute() (lines 219-223). Those minutes are applied to whichever invitee day contains the unadjusted override.start (the filter at lines 206-208), not the day of the shifted time. When the offset crosses midnight, the clock wraps onto the wrong day. Example: organizer Asia/Kolkata, override stored as 02:00Z-04:00Z meaning 02:00-04:00 local, attendee in UTC. The offset is -330 minutes, hour() becomes 20:30, and that is added to the UTC day of 02:00Z, so slots show at 20:30Z the same date instead of 20:30Z the previous day. If only the start wraps, startTime exceeds endTime. Organizer IST 09:00-18:00 viewed from America/New_York (offset -630 minutes) becomes start 22:30 and end 07:30. buildSlots drops any range with start >= end (line 68), but the override block has already removed that user's normal working hours (lines 228-245), so the attendee sees no slots on the override day.

Converted override minutes are shifted again for DST

Override bounds are converted to invitee-local minutes using utcOffset() of the override's own date (lines 212-223). buildSlots then runs every slot, including those override minutes, through getTime, which adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff (lines 102-110). That term corrects working hours that were converted with today's offset rather than the booking date's offset. Override minutes are already based on the booking date, so the extra term moves them whenever today's DST offset differs from the booking day's and the organizer and invitee are not on the same DST schedule. Example: organizer America/New_York, attendee in UTC, today in July (EDT, utcOffset -240) and the booking in January (EST, utcOffset -300). organizerDSTDiff is 60 and inviteeDSTDiff is 0, so every override slot is shown one hour late. Asia/Kolkata and Asia/Dhaka have no DST, so the new test does not catch this.

Override day comparison mixes server-local and UTC dates

Whether an override applies to a slot is decided by comparing formatted calendar dates (lines 110-111). slotStartTime is time.utc(), so its format() is the UTC date. The override side is dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") with no .utc(), so format() uses the Node process timezone. On any server whose TZ is not UTC, an adjusted override whose UTC date differs from the server-local date will not match the slot, and the fixed-host override is ignored or applied to the wrong day. Example: server in America/Los_Angeles, override adjusted to 02:00 UTC formats as the previous local evening while the slot formats as the UTC date. The check this PR adds then does not run.

Tests miss fixed-host overrides and timezone day boundaries

The only new assertion re-fetches a personal-event date override with the attendee in Asia/Dhaka (+6) instead of Asia/Kolkata (+5:30) and expects the same UTC slot list. A 30-minute offset does not cross midnight or a DST change, so it does not catch override slots landing on the wrong day, ranges with start after end being dropped, or the extra DST shift in getTime. There is no round-robin case with a fixed host and a date override, which is the behavior the PR says it fixes, and no case where an override day also has a booking or calendar busy time. createBookingScenario never installs the hosts/isFixed rows, so the new checkIfIsAvailable branches are not exercised and the double-book and split-window regressions would not fail CI.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount is a lost-update read-modify-write

Failures write retryCount to the value read at the start of the iteration plus one, instead of an atomic increment, and nothing claims the row (for example updateMany where id and scheduled false) before calling Twilio. This endpoint has no lock, and each reminder does several awaits, so a slow run overlaps the next cron tick. Both invocations can read the same retryCount, both call scheduleSMS, and both store the same next count. The new cap is then under-counted, so a reminder is attempted more than twice, and both runs can schedule a duplicate SMS. Use an atomic increment and a conditional update so a concurrent run cannot reset the counter or send twice.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem: retryCount is set to the read value + 1, which can lose updates when runs overlap, and both recommend an atomic increment. The candidate also mentions duplicate sends, but its core issue is identical to the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount cleanup deletes reminders this job does not own

The new deleteMany ORs a bare retryCount > 1 predicate that is not limited to method SMS, scheduled false, or unsent rows. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP, and the comment above the query still claims it only removes past-dated SMS reminders. Any row whose retryCount exceeds 1 is hard-deleted, including future email/WhatsApp reminders and rows already marked scheduled that still store a Twilio referenceId. Today only this handler writes the column, so non-SMS rows stay at 0 unless another writer sets them, but a concurrent cron can already produce a bad row: both runs load the same unscheduled reminder, one sets scheduled true and referenceId after a successful scheduleSMS, and the other writes retryCount from the stale in-memory value without touching scheduled. The next run then deletes that live provider message, so booking cancellation can no longer look up the SID and stop it. Scope the predicate to unscheduled SMS reminders.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same bug: the retryCount > 1 predicate in the deleteMany OR clause is not scoped to method SMS, so it deletes non-SMS (email/WhatsApp) reminders. The candidate adds extra detail about scheduled rows, but the core issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
Two transient errors permanently wipe pending SMS reminders

Every exception in the per-reminder try, and every falsy scheduleSMS result, increments retryCount, and the next cron deletes all rows with retryCount > 1. That includes Twilio timeouts, rate limits, and failures while loading the organizer profile or rendering the template, not only permanent rejections such as an invalid number. There is no backoff, so two consecutive runs during a short provider or DB outage set retryCount to 2 on every unscheduled SMS reminder in the 7-day window. The following run's deleteMany removes all of them. Those reminders are not recreated, the delete is not logged per id, and attendees never get the SMS after the provider recovers. Only permanent send failures should count, or the limit needs backoff before rows are deleted.

Unsendable reminders never increment retryCount

retryCount is updated only when scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws. If there is no destination (SMS_NUMBER sendTo empty, or booking.smsReminderNumber null) or the rendered message is empty, the handler skips the row and leaves retryCount at 0. The earlier continue when workflowStep or booking is missing does the same. Those rows stay scheduled false with a future scheduledDate, so every cron run loads them again until scheduledDate is in the past. That is the unbounded reschedule loop this change is meant to stop, and a booking with no phone number never enters the Twilio path the new counter covers. Treat these terminal cases as failures, or delete them, so they are retired after the same limit.

Failed retry bookkeeping aborts the rest of the batch

The new catch block awaits workflowReminder.update and does not handle that update failing. Previously the catch only logged, so the loop always continued. If the update throws — the row was already removed by this cleanup in an overlapping run, the reminder disappeared mid-batch, or the DB blipped — the exception escapes the for-loop, the handler 500s, and every later reminder in the batch is left unscheduled. findMany has no orderBy, so which reminders sit behind the failing row is undefined, and a cron retry hits the same hole. The original scheduling error is also never logged when the bookkeeping update throws. Ignore a missing row (or otherwise guard the update) so one bookkeeping failure cannot stop the rest of the batch.

Unparenthesized OR fragment breaks caller AND filters

In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, getBaseConditions returns the authorization fragment as-is when there are no service filters (line 75). Team and org scope build that fragment as `(teamPredicate) OR (userPredicate)` with no parentheses around the whole OR (the reduce at lines 171-174 and 204-207). SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so the intended caller query `WHERE ${await service.getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= ${start} AND "startTime" < ${end}` is parsed as team-bookings OR (personal-bookings AND date window). Every matching team booking is returned regardless of the date filter, and any other AND predicate appended by the caller (status, member, and so on) is skipped on the team-booking branch. That over-returns rows, ignores the insights time window, and can defeat caller-side restrictions. The same shape exists on the event-type filter at line 106 (`eventTypeId = X OR eventParentId = X`) if getFilterConditions is embedded directly. The old Prisma `AND: [...]` where input did not have this trap, and getBaseConditions already parenthesizes when it combines auth and filters (line 73) but not when it returns auth alone. Wrap every returned fragment, including the OR reduce result, in parentheses so external AND/OR composition is safe.

ANY() on a JS array is not a Postgres int array

In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, org and team authorization interpolate JavaScript number arrays into PostgreSQL ANY() at lines 164 (`"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})`), 168 (`"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})`), and 201 (`"userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})`). Prisma `$queryRaw` / `Prisma.sql` does not encode a JS array as a PostgreSQL `int[]`; the array is one untyped parameter, typically sent as text. PostgreSQL then fails the statement with an error such as `operator does not exist: integer = text` or `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side`. User scope only uses scalar binds, and the only test that executes SQL is user-scoped, so this is not caught. Team and org insights, the main authorization paths, will throw instead of returning bookings. Build the list with Prisma.join and an explicit cast, for example `"userId" = ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(userIds)}]::int[])`, and keep the empty-list guard because Prisma.join([]) is invalid SQL.

toEqual on nested Prisma.sql fragments will fail

In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts, the team-scope assertion at line 295, the org-scope assertion at line 332, and the combined-filter assertion at line 429 expect `toEqual` against one flat `Prisma.sql` template. The service does not build those fragments as a single template: buildTeamAuthorizationCondition, buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, and buildFilterConditions nest fragments with `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR/AND (${condition})``. Prisma stores nested `Sql` objects in `values` and only flattens them when the query runs, so Vitest deep equality fails even when the rendered SQL matches. Event create, update, delete, and contact sync fail for every Salesforce user as soon as this code runs, including deployments that never enable credential sync.

Token sync request sends user id with no authentication

The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug. It does not send CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, an HMAC, or any other credential, and it does not require the URL to be https. That endpoint is expected to return OAuth access tokens. The parent app therefore cannot tell Cal.com from any other caller who can reach the URL, and a client that can reach it can request tokens for arbitrary user ids. An http:// endpoint value would also put bearer tokens on the wire in cleartext. Nothing in .env.example says the caller is unauthenticated. The response is trusted with no status check, so an error body can be stored as a credential.

Lark deletes the credential before the sync refresh can run

refreshAccessToken still deletes the credential and throws when the stored refresh token is missing or refresh_expires_date is expired. That check runs before the new refreshOAuthTokens call. With credential sync the parent is the source of truth, and the sync helper documents a response that only contains an access token and expiry, so the local refresh token may be absent or already expired. In that case Cal.com deletes the Lark row instead of asking CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT for a new access token. The connection is gone and later calendar calls fail until the user reconnects; a webhook replay cannot help if the row was removed and a later findFirst misses the replacement.

Zoom sync asks for app slug zoomvideo but credentials are stored as zoom

Zoom's refresh calls refreshOAuthTokens with appSlug "zoomvideo", but the OAuth callback in this PR stores the credential with appId "zoom" and the install path uses slug "zoom". When credential sync is enabled, the parent is queried for zoomvideo and will not find the Zoom tokens it stored or received under zoom. Refresh fails and Zoom meetings cannot be created for synced users even when the webhook wrote a valid credential.

Credential sync upsert is racy and can leave a stale duplicate

The webhook does findFirst({userId, appId}) and then either updates that id or creates a row. Those steps are not in a transaction, and Credential has no unique constraint on (userId, appId). The Lark callback in this PR already notes that userId and type are not unique, which is why that flow updates by credential id. Two concurrent deliveries, including a parent retry, can both see no row and both insert, or findFirst can update an arbitrary duplicate because there is no orderBy. Calendar code also uses findFirst, so it can keep using a stale credential while the webhook returns 200. A retried sync therefore does not reliably make the parent the source of truth.

Synced credentials are not unmarked invalid

When a credential already exists, the webhook updates only key. It does not set invalid to false. Google, Webex, and Zoom in this PR set invalid true so a failed refresh stops being used. A parent that pushes a replacement token for a credential Cal.com already marked invalid still gets 200, but loaders that skip invalid rows will ignore the new keys and the integration stays disconnected.

Privileged credential webhook uses a raw reusable secret

This route can replace any user's integration credential, including calendar, video, CRM, and Stripe payment keys, for any app slug. The only check is inequality against a static header value. The compare is not constant-time, the secret is the raw header rather than an HMAC over the body, and there is no timestamp or nonce. A captured request stays valid forever and also discloses the secret itself, so the holder can forge new writes for every userId, not only replay one body. Rolling a rotated token back is enough to keep using a stolen OAuth refresh token after the parent thought it had replaced it.

No tests for credential sync or the OAuth refresh persistence change

The diff adds a privileged webhook and changes token refresh for every major OAuth app, but there are no new tests, and the PR checklist says tests were not added. The manual plan only hits the webhook and a simulated sync refresh. A unit test that refreshes Google and Office 365 with sharing disabled and asserts the stored key is still the token object, with the previous refresh_token kept when the provider omits one, would have caught the universal credential corruption. The webhook also has no coverage for a wrong secret, a non-object decrypted payload, an invalid credential being cleared, or two concurrent creates.

A single workflow delete can therefore enqueue one long-lived cancel per upcoming reminder and trip the cap for the whole platform. A cron invocation that starts at or after sendAt therefore destroys the only record that could still cancel the batch, and the email goes out. The new query only selects cancelled rows due within the next hour, and this job runs every 15 minutes, while SendGrid will not honor a cancel inside roughly the last 10 minutes before sendAt. A booking cancelled after the last successful tick (for example 10 minutes before the reminder) is not stopped, and the following run deletes the row instead of cancelling it. The loop at line 56 has no per-item try/catch and only awaits the Prisma deletes in Promise.all after every SendGrid call succeeds. If that POST fails, the helper swallows the error and does not set cancelled, so the cron will not retry and the old booking's workflow email is still sent after the reschedule. If those calls do not finish, the old reminders stay scheduled while the mutation also creates new ones, so both the old and the new messages go out.

This change replaces the SendGrid cancel-then-DELETE sequence and the awaited reminder deletes with a cancelled flag, a deferred cron cancel, and an immediateDelete mode, but adds no tests.
